article_content: Despite securing a $20 million settlement in 2004 against manufacturers of a butter popcorn flavoring, an event that should have guaranteed financial security, Eric and Cassandra Peoples from Missouri declared bankruptcy just eight years later. Eric Peoples contracted bronchiolitis obliterans, commonly known as 'popcorn lung,' due to exposure to diacetyl while working at a popcorn production facility in Jasper. This exposure led them to initiate legal action against International Flavors and Fragrances Inc. and Bush Boake Allen Inc. However, their fortunes took an unexpected turn for the worse. To settle debts, the couple was compelled to sell their custom-built residence, initially valued at $3.9 million. Records from the Joplin Globe indicate that the Peoples' property, including their home and 10.5 acres of land, was recently appraised at only $700,000. Additionally, their personal possessions were valued at approximately $33,000. Conversely, their liabilities exceeded $611,000, encompassing a $482,876 mortgage held by U.S. Bank. The Peoples' legal battle with the butter flavoring companies set a precedent, paving the way for similar suits from other affected workers and their families. Their claim asserted that Eric Peoples, a father of two, developed the debilitating lung condition following exposure to diacetyl, a chemical imparting the characteristic buttery flavor and scent. Research indicates that when diacetyl is heated, it transforms into a toxic gas with potentially fatal consequences, leading to symptoms like shortness of breath, persistent coughing, and wheezing. During the trial, medical experts testified that Eric Peoples would eventually require a double-lung transplant to survive. Adding to their woes, the couple faced a legal challenge from Jeff Neely, the contractor who spent five years constructing their home. Neely claimed they owed him $107,147, leading to a default judgment against the Peoples when they failed to respond to the lawsuit promptly. Although the jury awarded Eric Peoples $18 million and Cassandra $2 million, the precise amount the couple received after legal fees and other expenses remains undisclosed. Eric Peoples mentioned that his legal team would retain 35 percent of the award, and their attorney, Ken McClain, suggested some funds would be allocated to other workers involved in similar lawsuits. It's not entirely clear how the couple managed the remaining funds, but purchases included two Honda vehicles, a Chrysler PT Cruiser, and a Kawasaki Mule. Court documents also listed items such as a bedroom set, a dryer, end tables, china, lamps, a VCR, a microwave oven, and $50 worth of camera equipment. Since the settlement, Cassandra Peoples has worked as a realtor for Smith Midwest Realty and is involved with PJ's Country Bakery in Joplin, Missouri. The bankruptcy petition revealed an unsecured claim resulting from a November 2011 judgment in favor of Jeff Neely. The couple attempted to overturn the default judgment, citing difficulties, including Eric Peoples' declining health and asserting a counterclaim against Neely, arguing that the initial $400,000 estimate for the house construction ballooned to over $3.9 million. However, neither the motion nor the bankruptcy petition clarified the $3.2 million discrepancy between the construction cost and the property's current value. Bronchiolitis obliterans, or 'popcorn lung,' is primarily caused by inhaling airborne diacetyl, commonly used in microwaveable popcorn to mimic a butter-like taste. Scientists believe that heating diacetyl creates a hazardous, potentially lethal gas. This irreversible disease impacts the bronchioles, the lung's small airways, leading to narrowing due to scar tissue and inflammation. Symptoms include a dry cough, breathlessness, and wheezing, often culminating in the need for lung transplants. The disease gained notoriety when eight employees at the Gilster-Mary Lee popcorn plant in Jasper, Missouri, developed bronchiolitis obliterans in the late 1990s. Subsequently, in 2000, the Missouri Department of Health collaborated with the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) to investigate the cause and recommend preventive measures. Following a comprehensive evaluation of the plant and employees' medical records, NIOSH advocated for mandatory respiratory protection for all workers engaged in microwave popcorn production. In a separate case, in September, Wayne Watson, 59, from Denver, Colorado, was awarded $7.2 million after contracting the condition from consuming three bags of microwave popcorn daily. The jury determined that both the popcorn manufacturer and the retailer were negligent for failing to include warnings on the product labels about the dangers of diacetyl.
translated_content: Malgrat haver obtingut un acord de 20 milions de dòlars el 2004 contra els fabricants d'un aromatitzant de crispetes amb gust de mantega, un esdeveniment que hauria d'haver garantit la seguretat financera, Eric i Cassandra Peoples de Missouri es van declarar en fallida només vuit anys després. Eric Peoples va contreure bronquiolitis obliterant, coneguda comunament com a 'pulmó de les crispetes', a causa de l'exposició al diacetil mentre treballava en una fàbrica de crispetes a Jasper. Aquesta exposició els va portar a iniciar accions legals contra International Flavors and Fragrances Inc. i Bush Boake Allen Inc. No obstant això, la seva sort va fer un gir inesperat cap a pitjor. Per saldar deutes, la parella es va veure obligada a vendre la casa que s'havien fet construir, inicialment valorada en 3,9 milions de dòlars. Els registres del Joplin Globe indiquen que la propietat dels Peoples, incloent-hi la casa i 4,2 hectàrees de terreny, va ser valorada recentment en només 700.000 dòlars. A més, les seves pertinences personals van ser valorades en aproximadament 33.000 dòlars. Per contra, els seus deutes van superar els 611.000 dòlars, incloent-hi una hipoteca de 482.876 dòlars amb U.S. Bank. La batalla legal dels Peoples contra les empreses d'aromatitzants amb gust de mantega va establir un precedent, obrint el camí a demandes similars d'altres treballadors afectats i les seves famílies. La seva reclamació afirmava que Eric Peoples, pare de dos fills, va desenvolupar la debilitant afecció pulmonar després d'estar exposat al diacetil, un producte químic que proporciona el característic gust i aroma de mantega. La investigació indica que quan el diacetil s'escalfa, es transforma en un gas tòxic amb conseqüències potencialment mortals, provocant símptomes com ara falta d'alè, tos persistent i sibilàncies. Durant el judici, els experts mèdics van testificar que Eric Peoples eventualment necessitaria un trasplantament bipulmonar per sobreviure. A més dels seus problemes, la parella es va enfrontar a una reclamació judicial de Jeff Neely, el constructor que va passar cinc anys construint la seva casa. Neely va afirmar que li devien 107.147 dòlars, cosa que va portar a una sentència judicial per manca de compareixença contra els Peoples quan no van respondre a la demanda a temps. Tot i que el jurat va concedir a Eric Peoples 18 milions de dòlars i a Cassandra 2 milions de dòlars, l'import exacte que la parella va rebre després de pagar les despeses legals i altres despeses no s'ha revelat. Eric Peoples va esmentar que el seu equip legal retindria el 35 per cent de la indemnització, i el seu advocat, Ken McClain, va suggerir que alguns fons es destinarien a altres treballadors implicats en demandes similars. No està clar com la parella va gastar els diners restants, però van comprar dos vehicles Honda, un Chrysler PT Cruiser i un Kawasaki Mule. Els documents judicials també enumeraven articles com ara un dormitori complet, una assecadora, tauletes auxiliars, vaixella de porcellana, llums, un reproductor de vídeo, un microones i equip fotogràfic per valor de 50 dòlars. Des de l'acord, Cassandra Peoples ha treballat com a agent immobiliari per a Smith Midwest Realty i col·labora amb PJ's Country Bakery a Joplin, Missouri. La sol·licitud de fallida va revelar una reclamació sense garantia derivada d'una sentència de novembre de 2011 a favor de Jeff Neely. La parella va intentar anul·lar la sentència per manca de compareixença, al·legant dificultats, inclosa la salut deficient d'Eric Peoples, i va presentar una contrademanda contra Neely, argumentant que el pressupost inicial de 400.000 dòlars per a la construcció de la casa s'havia disparat a més de 3,9 milions de dòlars. No obstant això, ni la moció ni la sol·licitud de fallida van aclarir la discrepància de 3,2 milions de dòlars entre el cost de construcció i el valor actual de la propietat. La bronquiolitis obliterant, o 'pulmó de les crispetes', és causada principalment per la inhalació de diacetil suspès a l'aire, que s'utilitza habitualment en les crispetes per a microones per imitar el gust de la mantega. Els científics creuen que l'escalfament del diacetil crea un gas perillós, potencialment mortal. Aquesta malaltia irreversible afecta els bronquíols, les petites vies respiratòries dels pulmons, provocant-ne l'estrenyiment a causa del teixit cicatricial i la inflamació. Els símptomes inclouen tos seca, dificultat per respirar i sibilàncies, que sovint acaben requerint un trasplantament de pulmó. La malaltia va guanyar notorietat quan vuit empleats de la fàbrica de crispetes Gilster-Mary Lee a Jasper, Missouri, van desenvolupar bronquiolitis obliterant a finals de la dècada de 1990. Posteriorment, l'any 2000, el Departament de Salut de Missouri va col·laborar amb l'Institut Nacional per a la Seguretat i Salut Laboral (NIOSH) per investigar la causa i recomanar mesures preventives. Després d'una avaluació exhaustiva de la fàbrica i els registres mèdics dels empleats, NIOSH va recomanar l'ús obligatori d'equips de protecció respiratòria per a tots els treballadors dedicats a la producció de crispetes per a microones. En un cas a part, al setembre, Wayne Watson, de 59 anys, de Denver, Colorado, va rebre 7,2 milions de dòlars després de contraure la malaltia per menjar tres bosses de crispetes per a microones al dia. El jurat va dictaminar que tant el fabricant de crispetes com el venedor eren negligents per no incloure advertències a les etiquetes del producte sobre els perills del diacetil.

article_content: Ian Jones, a 45-year-old college tutor, has been warned he may face imprisonment after being convicted of simulating sexual acts with two students and grabbing the breasts of a teenage girl. Jones, from Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, targeted victims aged 16 to 21 while teaching a motor vehicle repair course at North Warwickshire and Hinckley College in Nuneaton, Warwickshire. The 45-year-old was on trial at Warwick Crown Court, facing 18 charges of sexual assault against five girls between 2008 and 2012. After deliberating for nine hours and 29 minutes, the jury found him guilty of five charges by majority verdict, but acquitted him of eight others. They were unable to reach verdicts on the remaining five counts. Prosecutor Graeme Simpson stated he would not seek a retrial on the unresolved matters, adding that the guilty verdicts adequately reflected Jones's conduct. During the trial, the court heard that Jones was arrested in 2012 following an incident involving a student at the college. Simpson told the court that Jones approached a student, placed his hand in her coat pocket, and touched the crotch of her jeans. When questioned, Jones claimed he was looking for cigarettes. The court also heard that when the student bent over to pick up her bag, Jones put his hands on her breasts and tried to pull her backward. The victim, left crying and shaken, reported the incident to the college's safeguarding team. Another female student subsequently came forward, describing how Jones simulated sex with her by approaching her from behind and pushing her so she was bending over. The court was also told of an incident where Jones grabbed a student's thong as she walked past, pulling it up and commenting on her green underwear. Jones, giving evidence, alleged that the victim was influenced by another student and had made a complaint to support her. Three other young women also came forward, and Jones was convicted of an offense against one of them. This victim stated that Jones made comments about her breasts, referring to them as 'a couple of airbags'. He also pushed her over a table from behind, pressed his groin against her backside, and smacked her with a ruler. Simpson argued that Jones's actions constituted bullying and an abuse of his position of trust, with each instance being overtly sexual. Jones was warned he faces jail at Warwick Crown Court and was granted bail until his sentencing next month. The judge ordered him to sign the sex offenders' register and requested an assessment of his potential dangerousness. Judge Alan Parker adjourned the case for sentencing, stating that while he didn't personally consider Jones dangerous, it was standard practice to assess dangerousness in cases involving convictions under the Sexual Offences Act. Jones, who was ordered to register as a sex offender, was granted bail but warned he faces a possible jail sentence. Judge Parker cautioned him not to assume any particular outcome, stating that he had an open mind. Jones is scheduled to be sentenced next month.

article_content: They say truth is stranger than fiction. This seems especially true after learning about these authors. Charles Dickens reportedly inspired Edgar Allan Poe's "The Raven". 1. Thomas Hardy: Upon his death on January 11, 1928, literary figures deemed British poet and novelist Thomas Hardy too important to be buried in his hometown's simple churchyard. However, the residents of Dorset, where Hardy lived for nearly 88 years, disagreed. A compromise was reached: Hardy's body was cremated, and his ashes were interred in Poet's Corner of Westminster Abbey. His heart was placed in a small casket and buried beside his first wife's grave in a Dorset churchyard. A rumor persists that his housekeeper's cat accidentally ate Hardy's heart, and a pig's heart was substituted. 2. Horatio Alger, Jr.: The author of over 120 "rags-to-riches" books featuring moral young heroes was also an admitted pederast. Before his writing success, Alger was a minister at a Unitarian Church in Brewster, Massachusetts, where he was accused of sexually assaulting two young boys. Alger admitted guilt but left town. He later moved to New York City, writing best-selling books for and about young boys that became popular in homes, schools, and church libraries across America. 3. Sherwood Anderson: Known for his short story collection, Winesburg, Ohio, and for mentoring literary giants like Hemingway, Faulkner, and Steinbeck, Anderson was known for sudden departures. In November 1912, while president of Anderson Manufacturing Co., he left his office to pursue writing. Years later, he made another abrupt exit during a South American voyage. At a farewell party, Anderson unknowingly swallowed a toothpick hidden in an hors d'oeuvre. The toothpick penetrated his intestines, causing peritonitis. He died in a Panama hospital. 4. Charles Dickens: Dickens had many pets, including dogs, cats, and ponies. His favorites were two ravens named Grip. He was devoted to Grip I, even writing the bird into his 1841 novel, Barnaby Rudge. This raven reportedly inspired Edgar Allan Poe's poem, "The Raven," published four years later. After Grip I's death, Dickens had him stuffed. Grip is now at the Free Library of Philadelphia's Rare Books Department, guarding the Poe and Dickens collections. 5. Flannery O'Connor: Like Dickens, O'Connor had a fondness for fowl. The author of "A Good Man Is Hard to Find" and "Everything That Rises Must Converge" loved birds from a young age. Growing up on her family's estate in Georgia, she played with chickens and reportedly taught one to walk backward, making it a local attraction. O'Connor especially loved peacocks, using them in her fiction to represent Christ. Returning to the family farm as an adult, she raised a large flock of peacocks, caring for them until her death in 1964. They were later donated to parks and monasteries but were all killed by predators. 6. O. Henry: O. Henry (William Sydney Porter) excelled at short stories but struggled with money. As a bank teller in Houston, he was accused of embezzling, leading to a quick move to Honduras. He returned to visit his dying wife but was arrested and sentenced to five years in prison. There, Porter adopted the pen name O. Henry. Prison provided writing time and exposure to interesting characters for his stories. He was released in 1901 after three years. He died in 1910 with 600 stories but only 33 cents. 7. Langston Hughes: Poet, playwright, novelist, and essayist Langston Hughes gained fame during the Harlem Renaissance. Before that, he worked menial jobs to support his writing. In 1925, while working at a restaurant in Washington D.C., Hughes placed poems under Vachel Lindsay's dinner plate. Lindsay shared the poems at his reading, and Hughes became Lindsay's "busboy poet." Hughes became a prolific author. Vachel Lindsay died six years later after drinking Lysol. 8. Edith Wharton: Edith Wharton, Pulitzer Prize winner for her 1920 novel, The Age of Innocence, is known for her stories about upper-class society in the late 19th century, a world she knew well. However, she also had a career as a humanitarian. During World War I, Wharton went to the Western Front in France to write and to help the Red Cross create hostels and schools for war refugees. In 1916, she received the Legion of Honor, France's highest civilian award. 9. Charlotte Bronte: Charlotte Bronte, author of Jane Eyre, had a tragic love life. In June 1854, she married her father's curate and became pregnant. During her pregnancy, she became ill, experiencing constant nausea and faintness, according to her biographer, Elizabeth Gaskell. She couldn't eat or smell food without becoming ill. On March 31, 1855, a dehydrated, malnourished, and exhausted Charlotte Bronte died at 38. For more mental_floss articles, visit mentalfloss.com . translated_content: 'Es diu que la veritat és més estranya que la ficció. Això sembla especialment cert després d'aprendre sobre aquests autors. Charles Dickens, segons es diu, va inspirar "El corb" d'Edgar Allan Poe.' '1. Thomas Hardy: Després de la seva mort l'11 de gener de 1928, les figures literàries van considerar que el poeta i novel·lista britànic Thomas Hardy era massa important per ser enterrat al cementiri senzill de la seva ciutat natal. No obstant això, els residents de Dorset, on Hardy va viure durant gairebé 88 anys, no hi estaven d'acord. Es va arribar a un compromís: el cos de Hardy va ser incinerat i les seves cendres van ser enterrades al Racó dels Poetes de l'Abadia de Westminster. El seu cor va ser col·locat en un petit taüt i enterrat al costat de la tomba de la seva primera esposa en un cementiri de Dorset. Persisteix el rumor que el gat de la seva mestressa va menjar accidentalment el cor de Hardy, i que el cor d'un porc va ser substituït per aquest.' '2. Horatio Alger, Jr.: L'autor de més de 120 llibres d''ascens social' amb joves herois morals també va ser un pederasta confés. Abans del seu èxit com a escriptor, Alger va ser ministre en una església unitària a Brewster, Massachusetts, on va ser acusat d'agredir sexualment dos nois joves. Alger va admetre la culpa però va marxar de la ciutat. Més tard es va traslladar a la ciutat de Nova York, escrivint llibres de gran èxit per i sobre nois joves que es van fer populars a les llars, escoles i biblioteques d'esglésies d'Amèrica.' '3. Sherwood Anderson: Conegut per la seva col·lecció de contes, Winesburg, Ohio, i per haver fet de mentor a gegants literaris com Hemingway, Faulkner i Steinbeck, Anderson era conegut per les seves sortides sobtades. Al novembre de 1912, mentre era president d'Anderson Manufacturing Co., va sortir del seu despatx per dedicar-se a l'escriptura. Anys més tard, va fer una altra sortida abrupta durant un viatge a Amèrica del Sud. En una festa de comiat, Anderson va empassar sense saber-ho un escuradents amagat en un aperitiu. L'escuradents va penetrar els seus intestins, causant peritonitis. Va morir en un hospital de Panamà.' '4. Charles Dickens: Dickens tenia moltes mascotes, incloent gossos, gats i ponis. Els seus preferits eren dos corbs anomenats Grip. Estava molt unit a Grip I, fins i tot va incloure l'ocell a la seva novel·la de 1841, Barnaby Rudge. Aquest corb, segons es diu, va inspirar el poema d'Edgar Allan Poe, "El corb", publicat quatre anys després. Després de la mort de Grip I, Dickens el va fer dissecà. Grip ara es troba al Departament de Llibres Rars de la Biblioteca Gratuïta de Filadèlfia, custodiant les col·leccions de Poe i Dickens.' '5. Flannery O'Connor: Com Dickens, O'Connor tenia una afició per les aus. L'autora de "Un home bo és difícil de trobar" i "Tot el que puja ha de convergir" va estimar els ocells des de ben jove. Criant-se a la finca de la seva família a Geòrgia, jugava amb els pollastres i, segons es diu, va ensenyar a un a caminar cap enrere, convertint-lo en una atracció local. O'Connor estimava especialment els paons, utilitzant-los a la seva ficció per representar a Crist. Tornant a la granja familiar com a adulta, va criar una gran bandada de paons, cuidant-los fins a la seva mort el 1964. Posteriorment van ser donats a parcs i monestirs, però tots van ser assassinats per depredadors.' '6. O. Henry: O. Henry (William Sydney Porter) va destacar en contes, però va tenir problemes amb els diners. Com a caixer de banc a Houston, va ser acusat de malversació, cosa que va provocar un trasllat ràpid a Hondures. Va tornar per visitar la seva esposa moribunda, però va ser arrestat i condemnat a cinc anys de presó. Allà, Porter va adoptar el pseudònim O. Henry. La presó li va proporcionar temps per escriure i l'oportunitat de conèixer personatges interessants per a les seves històries. Va ser alliberat el 1901 després de tres anys. Va morir el 1910 amb 600 històries, però només amb 33 cèntims.' '7. Langston Hughes: El poeta, dramaturg, novel·lista i assagista Langston Hughes va obtenir fama durant el Renaixement de Harlem. Abans d'això, va fer treballs manuals per mantenir la seva escriptura. El 1925, treballant en un restaurant a Washington D.C., Hughes va col·locar poemes sota el plat de Vachel Lindsay. Lindsay va compartir els poemes a la seva lectura i Hughes es va convertir en el "poeta cambrer" de Lindsay. Hughes es va convertir en un autor prolífic. Vachel Lindsay va morir sis anys després després de beure Lysol.' '8. Edith Wharton: Edith Wharton, guanyadora del Premi Pulitzer per la seva novel·la de 1920, L'edat de la innocència, és coneguda per les seves històries sobre la societat de classe alta a finals del segle XIX, un món que coneixia bé. No obstant això, també va tenir una carrera com a humanitària. Durant la Primera Guerra Mundial, Wharton va anar al front occidental a França per escriure i per ajudar la Creu Roja a crear albergs i escoles per a refugiats de guerra. El 1916, va rebre la Legió d'Honor, la condecoració civil més alta de França.' '9. Charlotte Bronte: Charlotte Bronte, autora de Jane Eyre, va tenir una vida amorosa tràgica. Al juny de 1854, es va casar amb el vicari del seu pare i va quedar embarassada. Durant el seu embaràs, es va posar malalta, experimentant nàusees constants i desmais, segons la seva biògrafa, Elizabeth Gaskell. No podia menjar ni olorar menjar sense posar-se malalta. El 31 de març de 1855, una Charlotte Bronte deshidratada, desnodrida i esgotada va morir als 38 anys.' 'Per obtenir més articles de mental_floss, visiteu mentalfloss.com . Copyright Mental Floss LLC. article_content: The article considers whether robots should possess rights similar to humans, including whether mistreating them should be permissible. These questions, often found in science fiction, may soon require real answers. According to the BBC, Kate Darling, a researcher at MIT, explores human interactions with robots, sometimes employing unconventional methods. Emotional connections with robots can be strong, raising ethical questions about their treatment, as MIT's Kate Darling observes. Participants in her experiments often hesitate to be cruel to robots, despite knowing they aren't alive. Is it time to consider robot rights? Watching a Pleo dinosaur robot seemingly suffer evokes considerable emotional responses. Darling's experiment involved allowing people to interact with a Pleo robot, designed as a children's toy. This cute, soft robot responds affectionately and requires guidance, similar to a newborn puppy. However, after an initial period of bonding, Darling instructs participants to use weapons to harm the robot. The resulting reactions were unexpectedly strong, with most participants refusing to comply. Darling believes our reactions to robots matter because advancing technology forces us to reconsider our relationship with them. She suggests that harming certain robots could become socially unacceptable, potentially necessitating 'robot rights'. While previously confined to science fiction, the idea of robot rights is gaining traction because modern robots are becoming more sophisticated. These 'social robots' exhibit autonomous behavior, mimicking pets or babies, thus triggering our emotions. Experiments have shown that even children struggle to mistreat robots programmed to express distress, such as a Furby. Similarly, soldiers sometimes award 'medals' to robots or hold funerals for them. One specific example involves a military robot designed to detonate landmines, highlighting the empathy humans can develop for these machines. Another experiment from the University of Duisburg-Essen tracked people’s reactions to videos of robotic pet abuse. Physiological and emotional responses were stronger than anticipated, even though viewers knew they were watching a robot.

article_content: Two knee surgeons in Belgium have identified a new body part: a previously unknown ligament in the human knee. These surgeons, from University Hospitals Leuven, hypothesize that their finding could explain why some individuals with repaired knee injuries experience instability during exercise. Orthopaedic surgeons Dr. Steven Claes and Professor Johan Bellemans researched anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears to understand why this injury sometimes causes the knee to give way. The surgeons discovered the previously unknown ligament, called the anterolateral ligament, in the center of the human knee. It is believed that 97 percent of people possess this ligament. The researchers investigated the injuries for four years, beginning with a study of an 1879 article by French surgeon Paul Segond, who speculated about an additional ligament in the front-center of the knee. They dissected 41 knees donated for medical research and confirmed Segond's speculation in all but one case. The Belgian surgeons are the first to definitively identify the anterolateral ligament (ALL). They suggest that ALL is present in 97% of human knees. After discovering the ligament, they aimed to determine its role in causing injured knees to give way. They found that injury to the ALL causes this phenomenon. This finding could revolutionize knee injury treatment. Dr. Claes and Professor Bellemans are developing a surgical technique to correct ALL injuries. Published in the Journal of Anatomy, the surgeons’ findings were praised by the Anatomical Society as ‘very refreshing’. The newly discovered ligament is thought to contribute to knee instability during exercise, a previously unexplained problem for many people with anterior cruciate ligament tears. The Anatomical Society commended the researchers for highlighting that, even with advanced technology, our knowledge of basic human anatomy remains incomplete. ACL tears are common among athletes in sports such as football, basketball, and skiing. The ACL is one of the four major ligaments in the knee and is critical for joint stability. An ACL tear often causes swelling, pain, and instability in the knee and frequently requires surgical treatment.

Després de descobrir el lligament, van intentar determinar el seu paper en fer que els genolls lesionats cedeixin. Van trobar que la lesió del LAL causa aquest fenomen. Les ruptures del LCA són comunes entre els atletes en esports com el futbol, el bàsquet i l'esquí. El LCA és un dels quatre lligaments principals del genoll i és fonamental per a l'estabilitat de l'articulació. Una ruptura del LCA sovint causa inflor, dolor i inestabilitat al genoll i amb freqüència requereix tractament quirúrgic.

article_content: The New York City Opera is in a precarious financial situation, needing to secure $7 million by the upcoming Monday to prevent a permanent shutdown. In addition to this critical sum, the opera aims to garner another $13 million before 2014 to sustain future performances, according to official statements. Risa Heller, the opera's spokesperson, informed CNN on Friday that failing to meet the $7 million target by Monday will force the board to initiate bankruptcy proceedings. To gather a portion of these funds, the company launched an online campaign on Kickstarter.com, seeking to raise $1 million by September 30. As of Friday, the Kickstarter initiative had accumulated $202,223 through contributions from over a thousand patrons. Heller also noted that the organization has independently secured $1.5 million outside of the Kickstarter campaign. George Steel, the company's general manager and artistic director, acknowledged the financial challenges in an online video, highlighting the significant progress made despite these hurdles. Nicknamed 'The People's Opera' by former NYC Mayor Fiorello LaGuardia, the opera was established with the goal of making opera accessible to all New Yorkers, as Steel explained. He pointed out that while a $600 ticket price would be necessary to break even, tickets are deliberately priced starting at $25 to ensure affordability. The New York City Opera has been celebrated for its groundbreaking premieres of works such as Robert Ward's 'The Crucible' and Anthony Davis' 'The Life and Times of Malcolm X.' The current season commenced on September 17 with 'Anna Nicole,' an opera that may be the company's last if sufficient funds are not raised by Monday. Steel urged New York residents and opera enthusiasts worldwide to support the opera, stating, 'We require the assistance of the very people we were created to serve in order to present our season this year. We are counting on your collective effort to ensure our future. I sincerely hope we can rely on your support.' This year marks the 70th anniversary of the New York City Opera, which was founded in 1943, making it the second-oldest opera house in the city, after the Metropolitan Opera, which was established over 60 years prior in 1880.

article_content: The Government’s Health and Social Care Bill became law today, after a difficult 14-month passage through Parliament. Deputy Speaker Lindsay Hoyle's announcement in the House of Commons that the Queen had granted Royal Assent to the bill was met with cries of 'shame' from opposition Labour MPs. The proposals were first presented in Parliament in January 2011 and were subjected to an unprecedented 'pause' last year as Health Secretary Andrew Lansley sought to secure the support of healthcare workers. Health workers demonstrated outside Parliament last week against the NHS reforms. The Health and Social Care Bill became law today. The reforms were amended more than 1,000 times during their passage through the House of Lords. The new rules allow the Government to create GP commissioning groups to purchase healthcare for patients and abolish Primary Care Trusts (PCTs). Labour has strongly opposed the new law, insisting it threatens the foundation of the NHS and could lead to excessive involvement of private services. Health Secretary Andrew Lansley faced significant backlash from doctors' unions. A draft risk register leaked today indicated that ministers were warned 18 months ago about the risk of the reforms leading to a loss of financial control, reduced productivity, and poorly managed emergencies. The Department of Health, which declined to comment on today’s leak, has resisted a ruling from the Information Commissioner to release the final version of the risk register in response to a freedom of information request from Labour. Shadow health secretary Andy Burnham said today’s document, published in The Guardian, showed that ministers were warned before they launched the Bill that it was 'likely to cause major damage to the NHS'. The document was produced on September 28, 2010, and it is not known what changes were made before the completion of the transition risk register on November 10. The Bill, which will devolve 60 per cent of the NHS’s budget to new GP-led consortia, has changed significantly since that date, with more than 1,000 amendments during its passage through Parliament. Identifying 43 separate areas of potential risk, the draft register rates each on a scale of one to five, where one means little likelihood and very low impact, and five means almost certain to occur and very high impact. The likelihood and impact figures are multiplied together to give an overall risk rating, with a maximum score of 25. Among 13 areas given a risk rating of 16 - with likelihood and impact each assessed at four out of five - were: Other dangers, considered to have a lower rating of 12, included the risk that 'the NHS's role in emergency preparedness/responsiveness is more difficult to manage through a more devolved organisation, and so emergencies are less well managed/mitigated'. The risk report warned that NHS emergency care could be more difficult to manage through a more devolved organisation. Staff concerns and union action over the reforms could lead to 'deterioration in relations, lower productivity in the Department of Health/NHS and delays in programme', the document said. And there was a warning that strategic health authorities and primary care trusts might lose “good people” who then have to be re-employed to run the new system. Mr. Burnham said: 'Now we know why David Cameron refused to publish the risk register before the Bill was through Parliament - it’s because civil servants were telling him his reorganisation was likely to cause major damage to the NHS. 'David Cameron will never be forgiven for knowingly taking these risks with the country’s best-loved institution.' A Department of Health spokesman said: 'We do not comment on leaks. We have always been open about risk and have published all relevant information in the impact assessments alongside the Bill. 'As the latest performance figures show, we are dealing with those risks, performance is improving - waiting times are down and mixed-sex wards are at an all-time low - and we are on course to make the efficiency savings that the NHS needs to safeguard it for the future.'
translated_content: La Llei de Sanitat i Atenció Social del Govern es va convertir en llei avui, després d'un difícil tràmit de 14 mesos al Parlament. L'anunci del vicepresident del Parlament, Lindsay Hoyle, a la Cambra dels Comuns que la Reina havia donat el Consentiment Reial al projecte de llei va ser rebut amb crits de 'vergonya' per part dels diputats laboristes de l'oposició. Les propostes van ser presentades per primera vegada al Parlament el gener de 2011 i van ser sotmeses a una 'pausa' sense precedents l'any passat mentre el secretari de Salut, Andrew Lansley, intentava assegurar-se el suport dels treballadors sanitaris. Els treballadors sanitaris es van manifestar la setmana passada davant del Parlament contra les reformes del NHS. La Llei de Sanitat i Atenció Social es va convertir en llei avui. Les reformes van ser modificades més de 1.000 vegades durant el seu tràmit a la Cambra dels Lords. Les noves normes permeten al Govern crear grups de comissionament de metges de capçalera per comprar assistència sanitària per als pacients i abolir els Primary Care Trusts (PCT). El partit laborista s'ha oposat fermament a la nova llei, insistint que amenaça els fonaments del NHS i podria conduir a una implicació excessiva dels serveis privats. El secretari de Salut, Andrew Lansley, va enfrontar-se a una important reacció negativa per part dels sindicats de metges. Un esborrany del registre de riscos filtrat avui va indicar que els ministres van ser advertits fa 18 mesos sobre el risc que les reformes conduïssin a una pèrdua de control financer, una reducció de la productivitat i emergències mal gestionades. El Departament de Salut, que es va negar a comentar la filtració d'avui, s'ha resistit a una resolució del Comissionat d'Informació per publicar la versió final del registre de riscos en resposta a una sol·licitud d'informació per part del Partit Laborista. El secretari de salut en l'ombra, Andy Burnham, va dir que el document d'avui, publicat a The Guardian, va mostrar que els ministres van ser advertits abans de llançar el projecte de llei que era 'probable que causés danys importants al NHS'. El document va ser produït el 28 de setembre de 2010, i no se sap quins canvis es van fer abans de la finalització del registre de riscos de transició el 10 de novembre. El projecte de llei, que transferirà el 60 per cent del pressupost del NHS a nous consorcis dirigits per metges de capçalera, ha canviat significativament des d'aquesta data, amb més de 1.000 modificacions durant el seu tràmit al Parlament. Identificant 43 àrees separades de risc potencial, l'esborrany del registre valora cadascuna en una escala de l'u al cinc, on un significa poca probabilitat i un impacte molt baix, i cinc significa gairebé segur que es produeixi i un impacte molt alt. Les xifres de probabilitat i impacte es multipliquen per donar una qualificació de risc global, amb una puntuació màxima de 25. Entre les 13 àrees amb una qualificació de risc de 16 (amb una probabilitat i un impacte avaluats en quatre de cinc) hi havia: Altres perills, considerats amb una qualificació inferior de 12, incloïen el risc que 'el paper del NHS en la preparació/resposta a emergències sigui més difícil de gestionar a través d'una organització més descentralitzada, de manera que les emergències es gestionin/mitiguin pitjor'. L'informe de riscos va advertir que l'atenció d'emergència del NHS podria ser més difícil de gestionar a través d'una organització més descentralitzada. Les preocupacions del personal i l'acció sindical sobre les reformes podrien conduir a un 'deteriorament de les relacions, una menor productivitat al Departament de Salut/NHS i retards en el programa', segons el document. I hi va haver una advertència que les autoritats sanitàries estratègiques i els Primary Care Trusts podrien perdre “gent bona” que després hauria de ser contractada de nou per executar el nou sistema. El Sr. Burnham va dir: 'Ara sabem per què David Cameron es va negar a publicar el registre de riscos abans que el projecte de llei passés pel Parlament: és perquè els funcionaris li deien que la seva reorganització probablement causaria danys importants al NHS. 'David Cameron mai no serà perdonat per haver assumit a consciència aquests riscos amb la institució més estimada del país.' Un portaveu del Departament de Salut va dir: 'No comentem les filtracions. Sempre hem estat oberts sobre el risc i hem publicat tota la informació rellevant a les avaluacions d'impacte juntament amb el projecte de llei. 'Com mostren les últimes xifres de rendiment, estem fent front a aquests riscos, el rendiment està millorant (els temps d'espera estan baixant i les sales mixtes estan al mínim històric) i estem en camí de fer els estalvis d'eficiència que el NHS necessita per salvaguardar-lo per al futur.'

article_content: Two men were sentenced to prison today for drugging and raping vulnerable, underage girls they encountered on the streets. Shazad Rehman, 30, received an 18-and-a-half-year sentence, while his nephew Bilal Hussain, 23, was sentenced to 17-and-a-half years at Bradford Crown Court. Judge Jonathan Rose stated that the men 'engaged in a course of conduct which has become increasingly and depressingly familiar in this country'. The defendants denied abusing the girls, who were picked up while frequenting the streets of Keighley and Halifax, West Yorkshire. A jury of eight men and two women found them guilty of multiple sex and drugs offenses after deliberating for two days. The court learned that Rehman and Hussain—known as 'Yaz and Naz'—plied the girls with alcohol and cannabis before taking them to hotels for sexual encounters. One 14-year-old girl testified that she felt ashamed, dirty, and worthless after being drugged and raped. According to Miss Colborne QC, Rehman boasted that his victims were ‘fresh meat’. She stated: 'They acted together, traveling from their respective home addresses in Leeds and Halifax to Keighley town center, where they specifically targeted vulnerable, underage girls.' She added that some of the girls, none of whom can be identified, came from difficult backgrounds or were emotionally fragile and possibly seeking attention. 'They were out of their depth,' the jury was told. 'They were supplied with strong alcohol and cannabis, enticed to believe they would have fun, that they were special.' 'In truth, what was on offer was beyond their control.' The trial revealed that one of the girls, who was 14 during the attacks in 2010 and 2011, was repeatedly raped. Prosecutors informed the jury that the men acted in concert and deliberately sought out vulnerable victims who had problems and were seeking attention. The men primarily targeted the Keighley area, using the Alder House Hotel in Batley and the Campanile Hotel in Bradford. Judge Rose told Rehman and Hussain: 'It is conduct which is pernicious, wicked, and determined.' 'It involved the deliberate targeting of young girls—girls who were already damaged, girls who were already very vulnerable, girls who were immature and seeking, perhaps, adventure, companionship, affection, and even love.' Bradford Crown Court heard how Rehman and Hussain—known as 'Yaz and Naz'—plied the girls with alcohol and cannabis and took them to hotels for sex. 'You two appeared in your fancy cars, with money to spend, compliments to pay, and with alcohol and drugs to entice these girls into those cars and to take them somewhere private and hidden, there to sexually violate, abuse, and degrade those girls until, bored, you sought what you, Shazad Rehman, described as ‘fresh meat, untouched and with no reputation’. Judge Jonathan Rose told Rehman and Hussain: 'It is conduct which is pernicious, wicked and determined' 'I have no shadow of doubt that you have caused incalculable psychological harm to your victims.' He continued: 'Neither of you lived in Keighley, but you identified that town as a place where you would easily find children who, unhappy at home and at school, would be easily persuaded to come with you for what they believed would be a fun and good time but was in fact nothing more than sordid sexual abuse.' Rehman, of no fixed address, was found guilty of raping two girls, sexual activity with one of the same girls, and sexually assaulting two different girls. Hussain, of Leeds, was found guilty of raping two girls and also of assaulting one of his victims. Both men were also convicted of a series of drugs offences and a charge of conspiring to intimidate a witness. Neither opted to give evidence during the trial, which lasted a number of weeks.

Va declarar: 'Van actuar junts, viatjant des de les seves respectives adreces a Leeds i Halifax fins al centre de Keighley, on van atacar específicament noies vulnerables i menors d'edat'. Va afegir que algunes de les noies, cap de les quals es pot identificar, provenien d'entorns difícils o eren emocionalment fràgils i possiblement buscaven atenció. 'Estaven fora del seu abast', va dir el jurat. 'Se'ls va subministrar alcohol fort i cànnabis, enganyades per creure que es divertirien, que eren especials'. 'En veritat, el que se'ls oferia estava fora del seu control'. El judici va revelar que una de les noies, que tenia 14 anys durant els atacs el 2010 i el 2011, va ser violada repetidament. Els fiscals van informar el jurat que els homes van actuar de comú acord i van buscar deliberadament víctimes vulnerables que tenien problemes i buscaven atenció. Els homes van atacar principalment la zona de Keighley, utilitzant l'Alder House Hotel a Batley i el Campanile Hotel a Bradford. El jutge Rose va dir a Rehman i Hussain: 'És una conducta perniciosa, malvada i decidida'. 'Va implicar l'atac deliberat a noies joves: noies que ja estaven danyades, noies que ja eren molt vulnerables, noies que eren immadures i que buscaven, potser, aventura, companyia, afecte i fins i tot amor'. El Tribunal de la Corona de Bradford va sentir com Rehman i Hussain, coneguts com a 'Yaz i Naz', van drogar les noies amb alcohol i cànnabis i les van portar a hotels per tenir sexe. 'Vosaltres dos vau aparèixer als vostres cotxes elegants, amb diners per gastar, compliments per fer i amb alcohol i drogues per atraure aquestes noies als cotxes i portar-les a algun lloc privat i amagat, allà per violar, abusar i degradar sexualment aquestes noies fins que, avorrits, vau buscar el que tu, Shazad Rehman, vas descriure com a 'carn fresca, intacta i sense reputació'. El jutge Jonathan Rose va dir a Rehman i Hussain: 'És una conducta perniciosa, malvada i decidida' 'No tinc cap dubte que heu causat un dany psicològic incalculable a les vostres víctimes'. Va continuar: 'Cap de vosaltres vivia a Keighley, però vau identificar aquesta ciutat com un lloc on fàcilment trobaríeu nens que, infeliços a casa i a l'escola, serien fàcilment persuadits de venir amb vosaltres pel que creien que seria un moment divertit i bo, però que de fet no era res més que un abús sexual sòrdid'. Rehman, sense domicili fix, va ser declarat culpable de violar dues noies, activitat sexual amb una de les mateixes noies i d'agredir sexualment dues noies diferents. Hussain, de Leeds, va ser declarat culpable de violar dues noies i també d'agredir una de les seves víctimes. Tots dos homes també van ser condemnats per una sèrie de delictes de drogues i un càrrec de conspiració per intimidar un testimoni. Cap dels dos va optar per declarar durant el judici, que va durar diverses setmanes.

article_content: I've spent much of my career climbing the corporate ladder. As chairman and CEO of Ogilvy & Mather, chairman of J. Walter Thompson, and later as Undersecretary of State to Colin Powell, I've witnessed how power is exercised and how people are chosen for leadership roles in corporations and governments. Despite an increase in talented women, they still hold relatively few positions of influence. Although I was a pioneering woman in a male-dominated world, I believe it's harder for women today to enter these influential circles. Men in leadership don't always know how to appraise women's potential. They understand that leadership requires competitiveness, resolve, and the ability to motivate. These qualities reflect a person's approach to work. Decision-makers can assess these characteristics in other men, but struggle to judge them in women, so they often choose familiar candidates – other men – for top positions. This is partly due to politically correct practices, which, while beneficial, have inadvertently created distance. Male leaders may not recognize intangible skills in women because relationships are more formal. Also, articulate, poised, and educated women are not always trained to enter the fray. Work can be personal, raw, aggressive, and unfair, with little immediate reward. However, handling these situations is part of leadership. These engagements require more than just great work skills and flawless logic. Women often excel at great work but may hide behind it instead of stepping up when leadership is needed. Women possess strong leadership qualities but struggle to communicate their unique approach to toughness and resilience. There's resistance when women overtly try to persuade, influence, or firmly press for unpopular decisions. It's harder to show leadership qualities over more accepted 'womanly ways,' like modesty. Women need to lead on their own terms. I'm not suggesting companies become 'kinder and gentler' or create special advantages for women. We don't need exceptions. Our approach is equally fierce, brave, and urgent, but we must unleash these passions from within. Women must identify and express their unique qualities. This is a crucial skill missing in many working women today. Only by understanding themselves can women see where their mastery lies. They must communicate their beliefs and what they offer. Despite being verbally skilled, women need communication skills to confront hostility, motivate, show purpose, and express anger. I teach these skills in 'The X Factor' workshops. We conclude with presentations, as work is a series of presentations. These can be emails, calls, meetings, or speeches, all opportunities to present oneself. Presenters can easily disappear behind charts or within the team. After our sessions, the mantra becomes 'Step out in front of the work.' It's rewarding to see women, once deferring to their PowerPoints, now step forward, willing to say 'I believe.' This is how a leader presents. When women communicate their leadership qualities, they'll be chosen to lead. I'm dedicating the next chapter of my life to helping women access this untapped power and reach their potential. I feel compelled because this handbook isn't available in bookstores or training courses, yet I wish I'd had it when I started in marketing. The opinions expressed are solely those of Charlotte Beers.
translated_content: He dedicat gran part de la meva carrera a pujar l'escala corporativa. Com a presidenta i CEO d'Ogilvy & Mather, presidenta de J. Walter Thompson, i més tard com a subsecretària d'Estat de Colin Powell, he estat testimoni de com s'exerceix el poder i com es tria la gent per als rols de lideratge a les corporacions i als governs. Malgrat que hi ha un augment de dones amb talent, encara ocupen relativament pocs llocs d'influència. Tot i que vaig ser una dona pionera en un món dominat per homes, crec que avui dia és més difícil per a les dones entrar en aquests cercles influents. Els homes en posicions de lideratge no sempre saben com avaluar el potencial de les dones. Entenen que el lideratge requereix competitivitat, resolució i la capacitat de motivar. Aquestes qualitats reflecteixen l'enfocament d'una persona cap a la feina. Els responsables de la presa de decisions poden avaluar aquestes característiques en altres homes, però tenen dificultats per jutjar-les en les dones, per tant, sovint trien candidats familiars – altres homes – per als llocs més alts. Això es deu en part a les pràctiques políticament correctes, que, tot i que beneficioses, han creat inadvertidament distància. És possible que els líders masculins no reconeguin les habilitats intangibles de les dones perquè les relacions són més formals. A més, les dones articulades, equilibrades i educades no sempre estan preparades per entrar en la batalla. La feina pot ser personal, crua, agressiva i injusta, amb poca recompensa immediata. No obstant això, gestionar aquestes situacions forma part del lideratge. Aquestes interaccions requereixen més que grans habilitats laborals i una lògica impecable. Les dones solen excel·lir en un gran treball, però poden amagar-se darrere d'ell en lloc d'avançar quan es necessita lideratge. Les dones posseeixen fortes qualitats de lideratge, però tenen dificultats per comunicar el seu enfocament únic de la duresa i la resiliència. Hi ha resistència quan les dones intenten obertament persuadir, influir o pressionar fermament per decisions impopulars. És més difícil mostrar qualitats de lideratge en comparació amb les maneres més acceptades socialment de 'dona', com la modèstia. Les dones han de liderar en els seus propis termes. No estic suggerint que les empreses es tornin 'més amables i suaus' ni que creïn avantatges especials per a les dones. No necessitem excepcions. El nostre enfocament és igual de ferotge, valent i urgent, però hem de desfermar aquestes passions des de dins. Les dones han d'identificar i expressar les seves qualitats úniques. Aquesta és una habilitat crucial que falta en moltes dones treballadores avui dia. Només entenent-se a si mateixes, les dones poden veure on rau el seu domini. Han de comunicar les seves creences i el que poden oferir. Tot i ser hàbils verbalment, les dones necessiten habilitats de comunicació per enfrontar-se a l'hostilitat, motivar, mostrar propòsit i expressar ira. Ensenyo aquestes habilitats als tallers 'The X Factor'. Concloem amb presentacions, ja que la feina és bàsicament una sèrie de presentacions. Aquestes poden ser correus electrònics, trucades, reunions o discursos, totes oportunitats per presentar-se. Els presentadors poden desaparèixer fàcilment darrere de gràfics o dins de l'equip. Després de les nostres sessions, el lema es converteix en 'Avançar davant de la feina'. És gratificant veure com les dones, que abans es refugiaven en les seves presentacions de PowerPoint, ara avancen, disposades a dir 'Crec'. Així és com es presenta un líder. Quan les dones comuniquin les seves qualitats de lideratge, seran triades per liderar. Estic dedicant el proper capítol de la meva vida a ajudar les dones a accedir a aquest poder latent i assolir el seu potencial. Em sento obligada perquè aquest manual no està disponible a les llibreries ni als cursos de formació, però m'hauria agradat tenir-lo quan vaig començar a treballar en el món del màrqueting. Les opinions expressades són únicament les de Charlotte Beers.

article_content: By Sam Adams. PUBLISHED: 10:31 EST, July 19, 2012 | UPDATED: 15:54 EST, July 19, 2012. A police officer is moved to tears as the grief-stricken parents of two-year-old Jamie Heaton, who died in a gas explosion, walk into their son's funeral service. Jamie Heaton was watching television when the blast occurred in Shaw, Oldham, on June 26. His parents, Michelle and Kenny, led approximately 400 mourners into the funeral at St James Church; hundreds more listened to the service outside. Tragic Loss: Jamie Heaton's parents arrive for the funeral. Emotional: An officer wipes a tear from his eye after the couple walks by. Jamie’s body was carried into the church in a small white coffin decorated with red, orange, purple, and green polka dots. Mr. Heaton, 36, and other male mourners wore ties with the same polka dot design, inspired by Mr. Tumble, Jamie’s favorite children’s TV character. Flowers spelled out 'Jamie' and 'Little Man' in red and orange. The theme song to Thomas The Tank Engine & Friends was played as the funeral began. Rev. Lynne Connolly led the service, noting the community's support since 'that horrible day.' 'The tragic death of Jamie has devastated us all,' she said. After the hymn 'Amazing Grace,' Jamie’s mother, Michelle, 31, read the poem 'Footprints.' The poem ended: 'My precious child, I love you and would never leave you. During your times of trial and suffering, when you see only one set of footprints, it was then that I carried you.' Mrs. Heaton, who works for Boots, survived the blast after stepping outside to hang laundry. The song 'You’ll Never Walk Alone' was then played. The explosion destroyed a house next door, killing Jamie, who was watching TV as his mother hung the washing out to dry. Tears: Kenny Heaton holds a tissue as he arrives for his son's funeral at St. James' Church in Shaw, Oldham. Grief-stricken: Kenny Heaton kisses Michelle. He and other male mourners wore polka dot ties as a tribute to Mr. Tumble. Dignified: Michelle and Kenny follow Jamie's coffin outside St James' Church. Colourful: The coffin is decorated with red, orange, purple, and green polka dots as a tribute to Jamie's favorite TV character, Mr. Tumble. Jamie died in an explosion that destroyed his family's home in Shaw, near Oldham. A 32-year-old man, believed to be a gas fitter, was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter and bailed until August 9. The Heatons' neighbor, Andrew Partington, 27, suffered serious burns and remains in serious condition at Wythenshawe hospital's burns unit. A male relative read a tribute on behalf of Jamie's parents, describing him as a 'happy little boy, mischievous and full of laughter.' The tribute continued: 'He loved watching Mr. Tumble every day. He loved being outdoors, going to the park, and playing on the slides.' 'He adored his family and his brother and sister, Jack and Jodie.' 'His personality was unique and amazing. We will miss everything about him.' 'Even though we only had a short time with him, the time we had was special, and his memory will live on through Jack and Jodie and everyone close to him.' 'Over the last few days, we have been allowed some quality time with Jamie, and he looked so peaceful and perfect. We take comfort in the fact that he passed away quickly and without much suffering.' 'He is in a safe place and we know he is being well looked after. We have no doubts that he will be up to mischief, looking down on us with that smile.' Mourners: People console each other outside the church. He added that Jamie's parents were 'overwhelmed' with the support they had received, thanking their families, the community, and emergency services. 'Our thoughts are also with the neighbors whose lives have been turned upside down,' he said. 'We are all going to miss our little man.' This picture shows the extent of the damage to neighbouring houses. Colourful: Jamie's name is spelled out in flowers. Moving: A tribute read by a relative described Jamie as 'a happy little boy, mischievous and full of laughter.' Heartwarming scene: Hundreds of well-wishers turned out to say farewell to Jamie. Bright: Jamie's personality was described as unique and amazing. Emergency workers: Ambulance crew workers were among the mourners. Emotional: Michelle read the poem 'Footprints.' 'És en un lloc segur i sabem que està ben cuidat. No dubtem que farà entremaliadures, mirant-nos des dalt amb aquell somriure.' Persones de dol: la gent es consola davant de l'església. article_content: Pakistani authorities have launched an investigation following the disappearance of two UNICEF personnel in Karachi, as confirmed by a United Nations representative on Sunday. The two employees were last seen on Thursday evening, according to United Nations spokesperson Vittorio Cammarota. Law enforcement is maintaining close contact with the families of the missing UNICEF workers, as stated by the spokesperson. Karachi, a major port city, serves as Pakistan's economic hub. Separately, on Saturday, a well-known Pakistani television news presenter was shot and injured in the same city. The news presenter's brother attributed the attack to the Pakistani intelligence agency (ISI), an allegation that military officials have refuted. Hamid Mir sustained three gunshot wounds inflicted by assailants in a vehicle and on motorcycles close to Karachi's airport, as reported by his media outlet, Geo News, which is affiliated with CNN. Amir Mir, the brother of the targeted news anchor and also a journalist, claimed that his brother believed the ISI, Pakistan's influential intelligence service, intended to assassinate him. The ISPR, the Pakistani military's public relations wing, issued a statement expressing regret and deeming it misleading to make unfounded accusations against the ISI or its leadership. The agency's spokesperson also denounced the attack in the same announcement, expressing hopes for Mir's swift and complete recovery.

Les forces de l'ordre es mantenen en estret contacte amb les famílies dels treballadors desapareguts d'UNICEF, segons ha declarat el portaveu. Karachi, una important ciutat portuària, és el centre econòmic del Pakistan. Amir Mir, el germà del presentador de notícies atacat i també periodista, va afirmar que el seu germà creia que l'ISI, el servei d'intel·ligència influent del Pakistan, tenia la intenció d'assassinar-lo. L'ISPR, l'ala de relacions públiques de l'exèrcit pakistanès, va emetre un comunicat en què expressava el seu lament i considerava enganyós fer acusacions infundades contra l'ISI o el seu lideratge. article_content: An Ebola outbreak has killed at least 59 people in Guinea, UNICEF reported, as the deadly hemorrhagic fever has quickly spread from southern communities in the West African nation. Experts in the country initially struggled to identify the disease. Symptoms, including diarrhea, vomiting, and fever, were first observed last month. Health Minister Remy Lamah stated on Saturday that initial test results confirmed the presence of a viral hemorrhagic fever, which the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention defines as a group of viruses affecting multiple organ systems. In a statement, UNICEF indicated that at least 59 of the 80 people who contracted Ebola have died, including at least three children. 'In Guinea, a country with a vulnerable medical infrastructure, an outbreak like this can be devastating,' said Dr. Mohamed Ag Ayoya, the UNICEF representative in Guinea. UNICEF has prepositioned supplies and increased communication to educate medical staff and local populations on preventing infection, Agoya added. The Guinean Health Ministry warned that the disease is primarily spread through contact with infected individuals, contaminated objects, or consumption of bushmeat. Most cases are currently in the forest area of southern Guinea. Health officials are providing free treatment for all patients and urging people to remain calm, practice hand hygiene, and report any suspected cases. The international medical charity Medecins Sans Frontieres announced on Saturday it was reinforcing its medical and logistics teams in Guinea to respond to the epidemic. It is also airlifting 33 tons of medicines and equipment and establishing isolation units in the three affected areas. 'Isolation units are essential to prevent the spread of this highly contagious disease,' stated Dr. Esther Sterk, MSF tropical medicine advisor. 'Specialized staff are providing care to patients displaying symptoms of infection.' Uganda declared the end of an Ebola outbreak in 2012.

Els experts del país van tenir dificultats inicialment per identificar la malaltia. Els símptomes, incloent diarrea, vòmits i febre, es van observar per primera vegada el mes passat. En un comunicat, UNICEF va indicar que almenys 59 de les 80 persones que van contreure l'Ebola han mort, incloent-hi almenys tres nens. Els funcionaris de salut estan proporcionant tractament gratuït per a tots els pacients i insten la gent a mantenir la calma, practicar la higiene de mans i notificar qualsevol cas sospitós. L'organització mèdica internacional Metges Sense Fronteres va anunciar dissabte que reforçava els seus equips mèdics i logístics a Guinea per respondre a l'epidèmia. També està transportant per via aèria 33 tones de medicaments i equips i establint unitats d'aïllament a les tres zones afectades. 'Les unitats d'aïllament són essencials per prevenir la propagació d'aquesta malaltia altament contagiosa', va declarar la Dra. Esther Sterk, assessora de medicina tropical de MSF. 'Personal especialitzat està brindant atenció als pacients que presenten símptomes d'infecció.' Uganda va declarar el final d'un brot d'Ebola el 2012.

article_content: Local police and federal authorities in Florida have arrested eight members of a white supremacist group, including three leaders, on charges of hate crime and conspiracy, according to police reports. Marcus Faella, his wife Patricia Faella, and Mark McGowan are identified as leaders of the local American Front organization. The remaining individuals are considered lower-ranking members. McGowan, 29, and his wife Jennifer, 25, are also accused of providing illegal paramilitary weapons training, knowing that these skills were likely to be used against the government, according to authorities. The arrests occurred over the weekend as part of a larger FBI investigation targeting white supremacist groups in central Florida, as reported by the Southern Poverty Law Center. The other individuals arrested over the weekend were: Diane Stevens, 28; Kent McLellan, 22; and Paul Jackson, 25. Christopher Brooks, 27, an ex-convict, was arrested on Monday. Police are also searching for Richard 'Swamp Nazi' Stockdale. All those arrested are reportedly members of the American Front in St Cloud, Florida. The organization describes its mission as the 'religious and cultural preservation of the European people,' according to the Orlando Sentinel. However, the Anti-Defamation League characterizes American Front as 'a racist skinhead group' with a history of violent crimes against Jews, immigrants, and other minorities. Prosecutors have further described the group as a 'domestic terror group.' All members were charged with committing a hate crime and criminal conspiracy. Marcus and Patricia Faella were released on Friday. Details regarding bail are pending confirmation. Marcus Faella has a long history of involvement in white supremacist groups in Florida. In the early 1990s, he was a member of the Confederate Hammerskins and led the chapter in Melbourne, Florida. In March, authorities arrested six people in Orlando who were members of the Outlaws Motorcycle Club and the 1st SS Kavallerie Brigade Motorcycle Division, which is also a white supremacist group. Police stated that those six individuals were plotting to blow up buildings and attack their enemies. Authorities have indicated that the March arrests and the recent arrests are likely linked to the same investigation, according to sources familiar with the case.

article_content: A New York man has started an online campaign this week to prevent the release of his mother's killers from prison on parole. Jason Minter was 6 years old when he witnessed his mother's rape and murder. The crime occurred 37 years prior to the original article's publication. His mother, Bonnie Minter, had brought him to a friend's house where his 3-year-old sister was having a playdate; the family interrupted a break-in. Witnessing the Horror: Jason Minter was just 6 years old when he witnessed his mother's grisly murder. He is now attempting to block her killers from being released on parole. Samuel Ayala, James Walls, and Willie Profit held Mrs. Minter, her friend Sheila Watson, and the children at gunpoint while they led them upstairs. The men put the children in one bedroom while they took the women to the other, raped them, and shot them dead. Though just a child, Mr. Minter tried to fight back and protect his mother. However, one of the men, Ayala, pushed a gun to his head and ordered: 'Shut the f*** up, kid'. 'The last words I heard my mother say were her begging for the lives of her children,' Mr. Minter wrote in an online campaign he launched last week. While all three men were given life sentences after the crime, they became eligible for parole in 2002 and have been applying for release every two years since. Campaign: Mr. Minter currently owns the Indian Road Cafe in Inwood, New York. As of Tuesday evening, his campaign had nearly reached its goal of 3,000 signatures. Up until now, they have been unsuccessful, but Mr. Minter fears that Ayala may be released this time since his family has begun writing on his behalf. 'He personally raped my mother. He personally shot my mother. He laughed about it as he left the house,' Minter told the New York Post. 'I heard him as he got into the (getaway) van and joked about his sexual prowess.' 'He thought it was funny,' Mr. Minter added. 'He’s a monster who should never get out of prison.' As of Tuesday night, Mr. Minter's campaign had nearly reached its goal of 3,000 signatures. He hopes the petition will stop the parole process once and for all. 'To have to do this every two years is torturous,' Mr. Minter told DNAinfo.

article_content: Billy Joe Donnelly, 22, was apprehended by police after he consumed part of a cucumber at the scene of a burglary, leaving crucial DNA evidence. Donnelly burgled a greenhouse and sampled the owner’s home-grown vegetables, leading to his capture. At Hull Crown Court, Judge Michael Mettyear sentenced him to two and a half years in jail, remarking, 'You were caught by a cucumber.' The incident occurred on August 21 when Donnelly not only ate various vegetables from the greenhouse but also burgled the adjacent home. According to prosecutor Jharna Jobes, the homeowner intended to sell the greenhouse produce, but found that someone had consumed a significant portion of the vegetables, including the incriminating cucumber. Jobes stated, 'A cucumber was found with his DNA on it.' The homeowners were asleep during the incident, suggesting premeditation. Donnelly then broke into the house by smashing a window, ransacked it, and stole valuable items, including the owner’s retirement watch. The wife later discovered their car was missing. In a victim impact statement, the couple expressed their intent to sell their home of over 20 years due to feeling unsafe. They stated, 'It has been very distressing,' and noted the sentimental value of stolen keyrings given by the wife’s mother after her father’s death in 1972. Donnelly, residing at Wimbourne Close, Bransholme, Hull, also stole £77 worth of meat from a shop. Upon his arrest on August 25, police discovered two cannabis plants in his airing cupboard. He pleaded guilty at Hull Crown Court to two counts of burglary, theft, and cannabis production. His barrister, Stephen Robinson, acknowledged the profound impact on the victims, stating, 'The burglary has had a profound effect on the complainants. He was just not thinking about that at the time.' Robinson added, 'He is sorry for what has happened and he bitterly regrets his actions.' He explained that Donnelly had been heavily drinking and, while riding his bike, entered the greenhouse and ate some of the produce. 'It was foolish behaviour and he was identified by a cucumber,' Robinson concluded. Donnelly has prior convictions for burglary and shoplifting. Judge Michael Mettyear sentenced Donnelly to two-and-a-half years in jail, emphasizing the seriousness of burglaries and their lasting impact on victims. 'Burglaries are regarded as serious by the courts because, often, people who are the victims sometimes never fully recover from what happens to them and they have been in this case,' the judge stated. 'They have been left so upset by what has happened they are going to have to move. It is absolutely ghastly and why courts regard it as so serious.' He concluded, 'I have absolutely no doubt you were out looking for something to do and the consequences have been ghastly,' adding that only a custodial sentence was justified, mitigated only by Donnelly’s guilty plea.

article_content: Winter storm Walda brought blizzard-like conditions to the Mountain West on Tuesday, with Colorado experiencing significant snowfall. Around 20 inches of snow fell in parts of Colorado. Denver International Airport had to cancel approximately 300 flights and cautioned passengers to anticipate potential delays due to de-icing operations. Authorities stated that commuter flights accounted for about half of the total cancellations. Numerous schools and government buildings were temporarily closed as a result of the heavy snowfall. In contrast, the East Coast enjoyed sunny skies and temperatures soared to 80F on Tuesday. Strong winds, reaching speeds of up to 70mph, impacted California, causing trees to fall and resulting in widespread power outages on Monday. Weather forecasters advised that severe dust storms could reduce visibility and create dangerous driving conditions in the area later in the day. Northern California was the first region to experience the storm's force on Monday, which subsequently extended into the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys. According to KGO-TV, at least a dozen trees were uprooted in San Francisco; police officer John Tozzini reported that over 20,000 utility customers lost electricity in the area. The Sacramento Bee reported substantial power disruptions within the Sacramento Municipal Utility District. The winds contributed to wildfires in some regions, including a fire in Fillmore, roughly 50 miles northwest of Los Angeles, which destroyed two homes and prompted the evacuation of 84 homes. Due to poor visibility, blowing dust led to the closure of state Route 14 in Antelope Valley, north of Los Angeles. Officer Michael Farrell mentioned that several vehicles collided with stationary cars on the road, but thankfully, there were no serious injuries reported. More than 13,000 Southern California residents lost power due to the strong winds. However, the surge of air had a positive effect: The Independent System Operator, California's main power grid manager, announced that turbines generated a record 4,196 megawatts on Sunday. The prior record was 3,944 megawatts, set on March 3. In Arizona, strong winds from a cold front blanketed Phoenix in dust and temporarily shut down 34 miles of Interstate 40 in the northern part of the state on Monday. At least four individuals sustained injuries in a pile-up involving two semi-trucks on I-10 in southern Arizona during a dust storm; none of the injuries were life-threatening.

article_content: By Simon Jones. Sunderland are targeting a move for Jack Rodwell, as the Manchester City midfielder seeks more first-team football. The 23-year-old has spent two seasons at the club, but has failed to make a significant impact under two managers at the Etihad Stadium, making just 26 appearances in all competitions and scoring twice. Rodwell was bought from Everton by Roberto Mancini for an initial fee of £12 million in 2012, but was hampered by a series of injuries and managed just 11 Premier League appearances. Wanted: Jack Rodwell is being chased by Sunderland. Rare outing: Rodwell shakes hands with Vincent Kompany following a League Cup tie with Leicester. His fortunes did not improve last season, with Manuel Pellegrini giving him just 10 games in all competitions. Rodwell has three caps for England, but only one came while he was at Manchester City - a substitute appearance during a 2-2 draw against Brazil at the Maracana in June. He is now being pursued by Sunderland, who are attempting to strengthen their squad after their dramatic Premier League survival last season.

article_content: Authorities are set to resume their search on Thursday morning at a pond in North Carolina, as the investigation into the disappearance of Private First Class Kelli Bordeaux from Fort Bragg continues. A tip led to the deployment of a dive team on Wednesday to a pond in Eastover, which is located near Fayetteville, according to Fayetteville Police Department spokesman Gavin MacRoberts. Police Chief Tom Bergamine stated on Wednesday evening that he couldn't provide details about the specific leads in the case. Detectives have interviewed one of the last known individuals who had contact with Bordeaux, according to the Police Chief. They are looking to speak with anyone who last saw her early Saturday morning. Police and military personnel also conducted a search in the vicinity of a Fayetteville bar, where Bordeaux was last seen and last used her mobile phone, officials reported. The 23-year-old soldier was last seen leaving Froggy Bottoms bar early Saturday, police have indicated. An anonymous Army official mentioned that Bordeaux had been drinking and received a ride from a bar employee. The same Army official added that Bordeaux sent two text messages. One of the messages said, 'got home safely.' The recipient and content of the second message remain unknown. Earlier on Wednesday, Bergamine informed reporters that the search areas are close to the bar and Interstate 295. Records show that Bordeaux's cell phone signal was detected near a cell tower early Saturday. Authorities have spoken with 'numerous individuals' as part of the inquiry into Bordeaux's disappearance, including her husband, who was not with her at the bar. Officers believe he was out of town at the time. When asked if police suspect Bordeaux is in danger, Bergamine responded that they are concerned because no one has heard from her. He also described her as 'a very good soldier' who wouldn't typically go AWOL or missing. Bergamine declined to answer several questions, including specifics about the text messages and whether Bordeaux is believed to be a random victim. He only stated that the case is classified as a missing-persons case, and many aspects remain unclear. The Army official mentioned that police searched Bordeaux's apartment and vehicle, but the official did not know the location where the vehicle was found. Bordeaux was reported missing on Monday when she didn't report for duty, according to the official. Her sister, Olivia Cox, told reporters on Tuesday that it was unusual for Bordeaux to miss work. Bordeaux's mother, Johnna Henson, mentioned that police informed her that someone gave Bordeaux a ride to the bar, where she participated in karaoke. Henson also told HLN's Jane Velez-Mitchell that her daughter felt 'spooked' during the ride home and asked to be let out before reaching her apartment. Henson does not believe her daughter made it home. Bordeaux is described as 5 feet tall, weighing 99 pounds, with blond hair and brown eyes. She was last seen wearing black shorts and a pink halter top, police stated. According to Fort Bragg spokeswoman Jackie Thomas, Bordeaux is from St. Cloud, Florida, and lives off base. Bordeaux is a health service specialist assigned to the 601st Area Support Medical Company, 261st Multifunctional Medical Battalion, 44th Medical Brigade. She and her civilian husband have been married for two years, according to her sister, Cox. The sisters last communicated on Friday. Cox said, 'I texted her. And we laughed and joked and everything was happy.' Police are urging anyone with information to contact Fayetteville police. CNN's Larry Shaughnessy contributed to this report.
