article_content: By Jaymi McCann PUBLISHED: 16:37 EST, June 21, 2013 | UPDATED: 05:53 EST, June 22, 2013 Competitive surfing was once considered a man’s world. But now, a group of Russian women have shown the boys how it's done, taking to their boards while wearing high heels. The women participated in a 'surfing in heels' competition in Bali on May 6. Scroll down for video. A group of Russian women went to Bali to compete in the surfing-in-high-heels competition. They showed the boys how to surf by taking to their boards with high heels on. One woman straps her board to her ankle above a black stiletto court shoe. The video was uploaded to Vimeo by Anna Lazar. A translation shows: 'Just yesterday we pierced the sand by the crystal-clear waters with our heels. To the sound of the crashing waves, the audience viewed the strange spectacle of chicks wearing high heels on surf boards.' The video shows them preparing for the competition by measuring their shoes. One surfer struggles to get to her feet as she reaches the crest of a wave. She begins to steady herself and rises slowly from the board. The competitor gives a thumbs up as she finally makes it to her feet. She launches herself into the water, celebrating surfing successfully in heels. The competitors also practice being in the water in heels by diving into swimming pools. Initially, the women look shaky on their boards, balancing on their heels and donning floral dresses. But they soon get the hang of it, surfing flawlessly and having fun. One competitor surfs wearing shocking pink strappy stiletto heels. The surfers all seemed to be having great fun competing in their high-heeled shoes. The competition attracted a large crowd of spectators and photographers. They are seen taping their shoes to their feet to stay on their boards. Some even manage to catch large waves during the competition. The video also provides an email address, appealing for future surfers. The next competition will be in October. Commenters expressed their delight at the video. Douglas Bland said: 'Classy... I'd love to share the waves with such elegance'. Alfredo Nuñez Plus wrote: 'Wowwwwww Anna amazing video, perfect shot and so good edited. Congratulation.;)' A blonde surfer gives a curtsey as she successfully navigates the wave. The women are forced to tape their shoes to their feet in an attempt to stay on their boards. Two competitors managed to catch a wave simultaneously while wearing their heels. There has previously been controversy in the surfing world, as the annual Californian surfing competition Mavericks refused to allow female competitors to enter. Organizer Jeff Clark told Jezebel: ‘We're not there.’ He noted that this year's event has 24 invited competitors and 17 alternates - all of whom have put time in learning to excel at Mavericks - while dozens more men would love to get in. ‘We've got one day to hold an event for the best of the best. If in 10 years there are 10 or 12 women surfers who surf Mavericks, who knows?’ The winner of the competition celebrates next to her surfboard. The entire team of competitors, judges, and spectators pose for a group shot at the end of a successful day.

article_content: A recent study suggests that shoppers are more likely to purchase a product advertised in an online classified ad if they believe the seller is white. A year-long experiment analyzing iPod sales on Craigslist in the U.S. demonstrated racial bias, with black sellers performing worse than their white counterparts. The research indicated that black sellers received fewer responses and lower offers for their iPods. Shoppers also showed less interest in white sellers displaying wrist tattoos. Researchers posted comparable photos of the devices being held by white and black men. To test for racial bias among buyers, U.S. researchers posted 1,200 classified ads in over 300 U.S. locations between March 2009 and March 2010. These ads featured similar photos of an iPod held by a man's hand, which was either black, white, or white with a wrist tattoo. The experiment revealed that black sellers received 13 percent fewer responses, 18 percent fewer offers, and offers that were 12 percent lower compared to those received by white sellers. White sellers with wrist tattoos experienced similar responses and offers. According to the study, published in the Economic Journal of the Royal Economic Society, buyers interacting with black sellers exhibited behaviors suggesting lower trust. They were 17 percent less likely to include their names, 44 percent less likely to agree to a proposed mail delivery, and 56 percent more likely to express concerns about making a long-distance payment. Professor Jennifer Doleac, assistant professor of public policy and economics at Virginia University, stated, 'We were really struck to find as much racial discrimination as we did.' She conducted the study with Luke C.D. Stein, assistant professor of finance at Arizona State University, during their doctoral studies in economics at Stanford University. The researchers placed their ads on over 300 local classified ad websites, which averaged 15.7 other ads for iPod Nanos the previous week. In more competitive markets with over 20 iPod ads, black sellers received a similar number of offers and equally high offers compared to white sellers. However, black sellers experienced 'particularly poor' outcomes in markets with fewer products for sale, where they received 23 percent fewer offers and best offers that were 12 percent lower. This news follows another recent study indicating that a person's race remains a significant factor in partner selection. Research analyzing preferences on the dating app Are You Interested (AYI) found that black men and women receive fewer responses to their messages. The study also found that black sellers performed worst in markets with high property crime rates and more racially segregated housing. This suggests that at least part of the explanation is 'statistical discrimination' - where race is used as a proxy for unobservable negative characteristics – rather than simply 'taste-based' discrimination, according to Professor Doleac. However, she noted, 'it is also possible that bias against black sellers is higher in high-crime or high-isolation markets.' The researchers also discovered that black sellers performed better in markets with larger black populations, 'suggesting that the disparities may be driven, in part, by buyers’ preference for own-race sellers,' according to the study. 'We believe our study isolates the effect of race on market outcomes more convincingly than previous studies and provides some insight into why buyers are discriminating,' Professor Doleac said. The dating app study also revealed that men from all races prefer partners of another race over their own. The study found that men respond to women approximately three times more often than women respond to men's messages, and that the women studied were primarily drawn to white men. The data originates from AYI, which claims to be one of the largest Facebook dating apps, boasting over 70 million users and bearing similarities to Tinder.
translated_content: Un estudi recent suggereix que els compradors són més propensos a comprar un producte anunciat en un anunci classificat en línia si creuen que el venedor és blanc. Un experiment d'un any que analitza les vendes d'iPods a Craigslist als EUA va demostrar un biaix racial, amb els venedors negres obtenint pitjors resultats que els seus homòlegs blancs. La investigació va indicar que els venedors negres van rebre menys respostes i ofertes més baixes per als seus iPods. Els compradors també van mostrar menys interès en els venedors blancs que mostraven tatuatges al canell. Els investigadors van publicar fotos comparables dels dispositius sostinguts per homes blancs i negres. Per provar el biaix racial entre els compradors, els investigadors nord-americans van publicar 1.200 anuncis classificats en més de 300 localitats dels EUA entre març de 2009 i març de 2010. Aquests anuncis presentaven fotos similars d'un iPod sostingut per la mà d'un home, que podia ser negre, blanc o blanc amb un tatuatge al canell. L'experiment va revelar que els venedors negres van rebre un 13% menys de respostes, un 18% menys d'ofertes i les ofertes van ser un 12% més baixes en comparació amb les dels venedors blancs. Els venedors blancs amb tatuatges al canell van experimentar respostes i ofertes similars. Segons l'estudi, publicat a l'Economic Journal of the Royal Economic Society, els compradors que interactuaven amb venedors negres van mostrar comportaments que suggerien menys confiança. Tenien un 17% menys de probabilitats d'incloure els seus noms, un 44% menys de probabilitats d'acceptar un lliurament per correu postal i un 56% més de probabilitats d'expressar preocupacions sobre com fer un pagament a distància. La professora Jennifer Doleac, professora assistent de política pública i economia a la Universitat de Virgínia, va declarar: 'Ens va sorprendre molt trobar tanta discriminació racial com vam trobar.' Va dur a terme l'estudi amb Luke C.D. Stein, professor assistent de finances a la Universitat Estatal d'Arizona, durant els seus estudis de doctorat en economia a la Universitat de Stanford. Els investigadors van col·locar els seus anuncis en més de 300 llocs web d'anuncis classificats locals, que tenien una mitjana de 15,7 altres anuncis d'iPod Nanos la setmana anterior. En mercats més competitius amb més de 20 anuncis d'iPod, els venedors negres van rebre un nombre similar d'ofertes i ofertes igualment bones en comparació amb els venedors blancs. No obstant això, els venedors negres van experimentar resultats 'particularment dolents' en mercats amb menys productes a la venda, on van rebre un 23% menys d'ofertes i les millors ofertes van ser un 12% més baixes. Aquesta notícia segueix un altre estudi recent que indica que la raça d'una persona continua sent un factor important en la selecció de parella. La investigació que analitza les preferències a l'aplicació de cites Are You Interested (AYI) va trobar que els homes i les dones negres reben menys respostes als seus missatges. L'estudi també va trobar que els venedors negres van obtenir els pitjors resultats en mercats amb altes taxes de delinqüència contra la propietat i habitatges més segregats racialment. Això suggereix que almenys part de l'explicació és la 'discriminació estadística' - on la raça s'utilitza com a representació de característiques negatives no observables - més que simplement la discriminació 'basada en el gust', segons la professora Doleac. No obstant això, va assenyalar, 'també és possible que el biaix contra els venedors negres sigui més alt en mercats amb alta delinqüència o aïllament elevat.' Els investigadors també van descobrir que els venedors negres van obtenir millors resultats en mercats amb poblacions negres més grans, 'cosa que suggereix que les disparitats poden ser impulsades, en part, per la preferència dels compradors pels venedors de la mateixa raça', segons l'estudi. 'Creiem que el nostre estudi aïlla l'efecte de la raça en els resultats del mercat de manera més convincent que els estudis anteriors i proporciona informació sobre per què els compradors discriminen', va dir la professora Doleac. L'estudi de l'aplicació de cites també va revelar que els homes de totes les races prefereixen parelles d'una altra raça per sobre de la seva. L'estudi va trobar que els homes responen a les dones aproximadament tres vegades més sovint que les dones responen als missatges dels homes, i que les dones estudiades se sentien atretes principalment per homes blancs. Les dades provenen d'AYI, que afirma ser una de les aplicacions de cites de Facebook més grans, amb més de 70 milions d'usuaris i que és similar a Tinder.

article_content: Fresh off winning a silver medal in the thrilling team Olympic equestrian event, Zara Phillips is likely elated. The Queen's granddaughter has a fitting vehicle to celebrate: a remarkable 26-ton, sky-blue 'super-lorry' that proved essential in her Games preparations. Phillips has been frequently seen driving the enormous Oakley Supremacy 'horsebox,' valued at £500,000. This vehicle comfortably accommodates both horses and their human companions. This transport method, favored by almost all of Zara's medal-winning team, provides sleeping quarters for six horses and six people. It features a double bed and a fully appointed bathroom with a shower, toilet, and 'his and hers' washbasins. The kitchen is equipped with modern conveniences, including a dishwasher, fridge, freezer, oven, and microwave. These appliances are neatly integrated into walnut cabinets beneath elegant granite countertops. A diesel hob is used for cooking. Perhaps the most striking feature is the air-conditioned living room, which can be extended for additional space. It boasts a plasma television with satellite access and a sound system for entertainment during long journeys to events. Measuring 39ft in length, the truck is equipped with rear-view cameras to aid in reversing, as well as cameras within each horsebox to monitor the animals. Zara, along with her teammates Mary King, Tina Cook, William Fox-Pitt, and Nicola Wilson, secured second place in the team eventing competition at Greenwich Park. The princess, married to rugby player Mike Tindall, follows in the footsteps of her father, Captain Mark Phillips, who was part of Britain's gold-winning team at the 1972 Munich Olympics. Her silver medal was presented by her mother, Princess Anne, who also competed in equestrian events at the Olympics, representing Great Britain at the 1976 Montreal Games.

article_content: Crystal Roles, despite years and miles of separation, still considers Naoma, West Virginia, her home. She left the mining town with her high school sweetheart shortly after their 1989 graduation and marriage. Each return home—to the area now under global scrutiny—is a reunion with a unique community for the coal miner's daughter. 'They're a special breed, unlike any other,' says Roles, 39. 'The people currently searching for the missing miners are those I attended high school with.' Authorities confirmed early Saturday the end of rescue efforts, with the discovery of the bodies of the four miners missing since the explosion nearly a week prior. The death toll from Monday's Upper Big Branch mine blast now stands at 29, marking the worst US mining disaster in almost four decades. Roles describes how rescue crews might have had 'to step over neighbors, church deacons, or recent porch-side tea companions.' The world now watches her hometown, but the story endures for mining communities long after the media departs. Rooted in family, hard work, and pride, it's a tale connecting generations. It's a life shaped by economic necessity—the need for work and family support—but it comes at a cost: mining is among America's most dangerous jobs. In West Virginia, the average miner earned $68,000 annually in 2007, according to figures from the National Mining Association. The organization states this was significantly higher than the average state wage at that time. Roles, now in Hickory, North Carolina, has closely followed the news due to her Naoma connection. She received immediate text updates from cousins Monday evening. Phone calls to her parents reveal her 63-year-old father, Benny Crum, is devastated. (See Roles' iReport posting.) 'I've been crying since this happened. My heart is broken,' said Crum, a former miner, Thursday night. 'Coal miners are like a fraternity. When one is hurt, we all hurt. You want to help.' Forced into retirement 18 years ago due to black lung, Crum feels helpless. Relying on oxygen, he listened to his scanner Monday night, watching and worrying as others rushed to the Upper Big Branch mine. Later, he observed a candlelight vigil from his porch. Mining was his passion, his only ambition. Roof bolting—securing ceilings for safety—was a dangerous 'drug' that fueled him during 18-hour days. His father began mining at 12, a day after his own father died on the job. 'My daddy mined for 57 years, mostly underground,' Crum said. Crum notes that miners defy stereotypes. They include teachers, ministers, and police officers—trained individuals who choose mining out of pride or economic necessity. Crum recalls miners leaving for medical school, stating, 'They're not doing this because they're too stupid. They're skilled, educated—not just hicks.' Those connected to mining communities emphasize an unparalleled work ethic. Brian, Kara Scurlock's 31-year-old husband, works in a mine near Upper Big Branch for about nine hours a day, six days a week. Vacation is nonexistent. Including travel, he's gone roughly 12 hours daily. (See Kara Scurlock's iReport posting.) Deep underground, the ceiling is about 3 feet high. 'It's cold, wet, muddy. They're sore, tired, hunched over,' she said. 'His knees pop when he walks, and he's always congested, constantly hacking.' Yet, her husband doesn't complain. He improved their home in his free time. After his brother, Rodney, was electrocuted in the same Massey Energy mine in 2003, he took time off, but returned soon after marrying Kara in 2005. 'It gets in your blood,' said Scurlock, a granddaughter and great-granddaughter of miners. 'I support whatever he chooses.' Scurlock worries, but her husband shows no fear. On Monday night, she held him and cried. Every workday is the same, she says: 'He kisses me, says he loves me, and I make him carry a pen and paper in his bucket, just in case.' Country singer Kathy Mattea maintains a deep connection with mining families. Her grandfathers were West Virginia miners. One organized for the United Mine Workers of America in the 1920s and '30s. The news triggered 'unexplainable grief for people I've never met.' The 2006 Sago Mine disaster inspired her 2008 album 'Coal.' Mattea, who was 9 during the 1968 Farmington, West Virginia, explosion that killed 78 miners, remembers 'the pall over our household.' Mine disasters always evoke that memory. She honors her mining history with simple actions and encourages others to do the same. 'When we flip on a light switch, we're part of the story,' said Mattea, from Nashville, Tennessee. 'Yesterday was hot enough for AC. Because I'm doing this, I'm linked to what's happening there. It felt different.'
translated_content: Crystal Roles, malgrat els anys i els quilòmetres de distància, encara considera Naoma, Virgínia de l'Oest, casa seva. Va deixar la ciutat minera amb el seu amor de l'institut poc després de graduar-se i casar-se el 1989. Cada retorn a casa—a la zona ara sota escrutini global—és una reunió amb una comunitat única per a la filla d'un miner del carbó. 'Són una raça especial, diferent de qualsevol altra,' diu Roles, de 39 anys. 'La gent que actualment busca els miners desapareguts són aquells amb qui anava a l'institut.' Les autoritats van confirmar dissabte d'hora el final dels esforços de rescat, amb el descobriment dels cossos dels quatre miners desapareguts des de l'explosió de feia gairebé una setmana. El nombre de morts per l'explosió de dilluns a la mina Upper Big Branch ara és de 29, marcant el pitjor desastre miner als EUA en gairebé quatre dècades. Roles descriu com les tripulacions de rescat podrien haver 'hagut de trepitjar veïns, diaques de l'església o persones amb qui feia poc havien compartit una estona al porxo prenent el te.' El món ara observa la seva ciutat natal, però la història perdura per a les comunitats mineres molt després que els mitjans de comunicació marxin. Arrelada en la família, el treball dur i l'orgull, és una història que connecta generacions. És una vida modelada per la necessitat econòmica—la necessitat de treball i suport familiar—però té un cost: la mineria és un dels treballs més perillosos d'Amèrica. A Virgínia de l'Oest, el miner mitjà guanyava 68.000 dòlars anuals el 2007, segons les xifres de l'Associació Nacional de Mineria. L'organització afirma que aquesta xifra era significativament superior al salari mitjà estatal en aquell moment. Roles, ara a Hickory, Carolina del Nord, ha seguit de prop les notícies a causa de la seva connexió amb Naoma. Va rebre actualitzacions de text immediates dels cosins dilluns al vespre. Les trucades als seus pares revelen que el seu pare, Benny Crum, de 63 anys, està devastat. (Vegeu la publicació iReport de Roles.) 'He estat plorant des que va passar això. Tinc el cor trencat,' va dir Crum, un antic miner, dijous a la nit. 'Els miners del carbó són com una fraternitat. Quan un es fa mal, tots ens fem mal. Volem ajudar.' Forçat a la jubilació fa 18 anys a causa de la pneumoconiosi, Crum se sent impotent. Depenent de l'oxigen, va escoltar el seu escàner dilluns a la nit, observant i preocupant-se mentre altres corrien cap a la mina Upper Big Branch. Més tard, va observar una vetlla a la llum de les espelmes des del seu porxo. La mineria era la seva passió, la seva única ambició. L'apuntalament de sostres—assegurar els sostres per seguretat—era una 'droga' perillosa que el motivava durant jornades de 18 hores. El seu pare va començar a treballar a les mines als 12 anys, l'endemà que el seu propi pare morís a la feina. 'El meu pare va treballar a la mina durant 57 anys, sobretot sota terra,' va dir Crum. Crum assenyala que els miners desafien els estereotips. Entre ells hi ha mestres, ministres i agents de policia—individus formats que trien la mineria per orgull o per necessitat econòmica. Crum recorda miners que van marxar a estudiar medicina, afirmant: 'No fan això perquè siguin massa estúpids. Són gent qualificada, educada—no pas uns qualsevol.' Els qui estan connectats a les comunitats mineres remarquen una ètica de treball incomparable. Brian, el marit de Kara Scurlock, de 31 anys, treballa en una mina prop de Upper Big Branch durant unes nou hores al dia, sis dies a la setmana. Les vacances són inexistents. Comptant el viatge, està fora de casa aproximadament 12 hores diàries. (Vegeu la publicació iReport de Kara Scurlock.) Molt a sota terra, el sostre fa uns 90 centímetres d'alçada. 'Fa fred, hi ha humitat, hi ha fang. Estan adolorits, cansats, encorbats,' va dir ella. 'Els genolls li cruixen quan camina, i sempre està congestionat, tossint contínuament.' Tot i així, el seu marit no es queixa. Ha millorat la casa en el seu temps lliure. Després que el seu germà, Rodney, fos electrocutat a la mateixa mina de Massey Energy el 2003, va agafar-se un temps lliure, però va tornar-hi poc després de casar-se amb Kara el 2005. 'Et corre per la sang,' va dir Scurlock, néta i besnéta de miners. 'Li dono suport faci el que faci.' Scurlock es preocupa, però el seu marit no mostra por. Dilluns a la nit, el va abraçar i va plorar. Cada dia que marxa a treballar és igual, diu ella: 'Em fa un petó, em diu que m'estima, i faig que porti un bolígraf i un paper a la carmanyola, per si de cas.' La cantant de country Kathy Mattea manté una connexió profunda amb les famílies mineres. Els seus avis eren miners de Virgínia de l'Oest. Un va ser organitzador per als United Mine Workers of America a les dècades de 1920 i 30. La notícia va desencadenar 'un dolor inexplicable per gent que no he conegut mai.' El desastre de la mina Sago del 2006 va inspirar el seu àlbum 'Coal' del 2008. Mattea, que tenia 9 anys durant l'explosió de Farmington, Virgínia de l'Oest, el 1968 que va matar 78 miners, recorda 'l'ombra que va planar sobre casa nostra.' Els desastres miners sempre evoquen aquest record. Ella honra la seva història minera amb accions senzilles i anima els altres a fer el mateix. 'Quan encenem un interruptor, formem part de la història,' va dir Mattea, de Nashville, Tennessee. 'Ahir feia prou calor per posar l'aire condicionat. Com que estic fent això, estic connectada amb el que està passant allà. Vaig sentir-ho d'una manera diferent.'

article_content: By Gemma Mullin for MailOnline. A team of refuse collectors accidentally dumped a large pile of garbage onto a busy high street during rush hour. The incident occurred on Shirley Road in Southampton around 8 am when a refuse truck malfunctioned while collecting wheelie bins from local businesses, emptying its entire load onto the road. The crew spent over an hour shoveling the debris with a mechanical street sweeper, resulting in significant traffic delays for commuters. A refuse worker stood by the truck, which malfunctioned and released its contents onto Shirley Road in Southampton during the morning rush, disrupting traffic. Southampton City Council has initiated an investigation into the event and is examining its fleet of similar vehicles. Steve Locke, who manages a recruitment firm on the street, commented: 'It was quite funny, to be honest. I don’t believe it was anyone’s fault. The workers rushed to press the stop button, but it didn't stop unloading. There was nothing anyone could do.' Benedict Carey, who filmed the scene with his phone, stated: 'It was certainly a strange sight. I asked the operators “okay, who pressed the wrong button?” They replied that it wasn’t possible and that “city council cutbacks” were to blame. They seemed to be in good spirits about it all.' The arrival of a JCB expedited the cleanup, successfully clearing the road. A statement from Southampton City Council read: 'The waste that was accidentally dropped has now been cleared, and our staff responded immediately to minimize disruption to residents. We will investigate the cause of the vehicle failure immediately. Once we determine the cause, we will inspect other vehicles to ensure this remains an isolated incident.'

article_content: New regulations are set to be implemented, stipulating that foreign migrants must earn a minimum of £149 weekly to be eligible for benefits. These rules were announced on February 18, 2014. Starting March 1st, individuals from European nations who claim to have worked or been self-employed to gain access to a broader spectrum of benefits will encounter a more rigorous evaluation. Current EU law's definition of 'worker' is expansive. This allows those working only briefly, like a few hours weekly at a pub, to receive Housing Benefit, Child Benefit, and Child Tax Credits. The definition of 'worker' will be redefined to be more restrictive. To demonstrate genuine work in the UK, a European migrant must prove consistent earnings equivalent to those paying National Insurance for the prior three months. This threshold equates to working 24 hours a week at minimum wage. Those meeting the 'worker' criteria can claim benefits, including JobSeeker’s Allowance if unemployed, as well as Income Support and Employment and Support Allowance. Those not meeting the income requirement will be classified as jobseekers or economically inactive. They must wait three months after seeking employment before claiming JSA and Housing Benefit (from April 1st). Work and Pensions Secretary Iain Duncan Smith stated these measures ensure the economy benefits diligent individuals who contribute to the country and abide by regulations. He added that these changes guarantee a fair system. This system supports genuine workers and jobseekers, while preventing exploitation of the benefits system. Duncan Smith noted that the public rightfully expects migrants to contribute, rather than be drawn by attractive benefits. The new laws will particularly scrutinize migrants to prevent 'benefit tourism' from new EU member countries. The minimum income requirement will remain linked to the National Insurance Contributions Threshold. This was £149 weekly (£7755 yearly) in 2013/14, and £153 weekly (£7956 yearly) in 2014/15. These changes follow David Cameron's call for stricter benefit system measures in 2013. He emphasized action due to concerns that lifting restrictions on Bulgarian and Romanian arrivals (January 1st, 2014) would cause a migrant surge. Since January 1st, 2014, EEA migrants face a stricter 'habitual residence test' and a three-month wait for income-based JSA. If they pass, JSA is limited to 6 months. After this, only those with a job offer or strong job-finding prospects can continue claiming. A DWP source said this is part of a plan to cap welfare, reduce immigration, and ensure the economy supports active contributors.

Aquestes normes es van anunciar el 18 de febrer de 2014. A partir de l'1 de març, les persones de països europeus que afirmin haver treballat o estat autònomes per accedir a un ventall més ampli de prestacions s'enfrontaran a una avaluació més rigorosa. La definició actual de 'treballador' segons la legislació de la UE és àmplia. La definició de 'treballador' es redefinirà per ser més restrictiva. Per demostrar un treball genuí al Regne Unit, un migrant europeu ha de demostrar uns ingressos consistents equivalents als que paguen les cotitzacions a la Seguretat Social durant els tres mesos anteriors. Aquest llindar equival a treballar 24 hores setmanals amb el salari mínim. Les persones que compleixin els criteris de 'treballador' poden sol·licitar prestacions, incloent-hi l'ajut de cerca de feina si estan sense feina, així com l'ajut d'ingressos i l'ajut d'ocupació i suport. Les persones que no compleixin el requisit d'ingressos es classificaran com a sol·licitants de feina o econòmicament inactives. El secretari de Treball i Pensions, Iain Duncan Smith, va declarar que aquestes mesures garanteixen que l'economia beneficiï les persones diligents que contribueixen al país i compleixen les normes. Va afegir que aquests canvis garanteixen un sistema just. Aquest sistema dóna suport als treballadors i demandants de feina genuïns, alhora que evita l'explotació del sistema de prestacions. Duncan Smith va assenyalar que el públic espera amb raó que els migrants contribueixin, en lloc de ser atrets per les prestacions. Les noves lleis analitzaran particularment els migrants per evitar el 'turisme de prestacions' dels nous països membres de la UE. El requisit d'ingressos mínims seguirà vinculat al llindar de les cotitzacions a la Seguretat Social. Aquest va ser de 149 £ setmanals (7755 £ anuals) el 2013/14, i de 153 £ setmanals (7956 £ anuals) el 2014/15. Aquests canvis segueixen la crida de David Cameron per a mesures més estrictes del sistema de prestacions el 2013. Va destacar la necessitat d'actuar a causa de les preocupacions que l'aixecament de les restriccions a les arribades de ciutadans búlgars i romanesos (1 de gener de 2014) provocaria una onada migratòria. Des de l'1 de gener de 2014, els migrants de l'EEE s'enfronten a una 'prova de residència habitual' més estricta i a una espera de tres mesos per a l'ajut JSA basat en els ingressos. Si l'aproven, el JSA es limita a 6 mesos. Després d'això, només aquelles persones que tinguin una oferta de feina o unes perspectives reals de trobar feina poden continuar reclamant. Una font del DWP va dir que això forma part d'un pla per limitar el benestar social, reduir la immigració i garantir que l'economia doni suport als contribuents actius.

article_content: Christmas dinner can be a stressful affair, as thousands of amateur cooks across the country attempt to perfect the festive roast. So, why not simplify things by popping one of these Christmas dinner pies in the oven on the big day? Inspired by a traditional pork pie, this impressive creation contains everything needed for a complete roast dinner, including potatoes, Brussels sprouts, chipolatas, turkey, and even a miniature Christmas pudding at its center. Sarah Pettegree, the founder of Bray's Pork Pies in Norfolk, created the Christmas dinner pie. From bottom to top, it contains: Cranberry sauce, chipolatas, Brussels sprouts, turkey, carrots, potatoes, parsnips, and roasted onions, with a Christmas pudding centre. The only addition needed is gravy, as the pork pastry also contains cranberry sauce. Veteran pie maker Sarah Pettegree conceived the idea after a day filming with the famously experimental chef, Heston Blumenthal. She said: 'When I was given a commission to make a one-off pork pie with a full Christmas lunch, I was undaunted and decided to think like Heston.' Bray's is renowned for its variety of unusual creations, such as onion marmalade, chilli, chorizo, and fig and orange. Sarah says she was inspired to make the pie by the famously inventive chef Heston Blumenthal. 'This was definitely a one-off for this year, but if there's enough demand, we might consider supplying people's full Christmas lunch in a pastry case next year.' 'It would certainly cut down on the washing-up time on Christmas Day.' Ms. Pettegree is the founder of Bray's Cottage Pork Pies, based on the North Norfolk coast, and is an expert in experimental pork pie creations. The pie's exterior is made from a traditional hot water crust pastry, while the pudding is covered with suet. For those seeking a hassle-free Christmas morning or aiming to reduce washing up, this pie is an ideal solution. The company is famous for its unusual approach to pork pies and sells its varieties, including onion marmalade, chilli, chorizo, and fig and orange, in delis and pubs across the UK. In the past, Sarah has made one-off pork pies with luxurious black truffles, regularly creates wedding pork pies, and even made a large UK-shaped pork pie.

article_content: Sir Douglas Bader was Britain's most celebrated pilot of the Second World War. Despite losing both legs in a plane crash, he continued to serve and helped the Allies defeat the Germans in the air. However, a new documentary confirms his aerial brilliance but challenges Sir Douglas Bader's 'Big Wing' tactics, which involved using up to 60 RAF planes to overwhelm the enemy in a large formation. Veterans who served with him suggest that this approach was slow and endangered other pilots. Wing Commander Tom Neil, 93, a recipient of the Distinguished Flying Cross and Bar with 15 confirmed kills, participated in the 'Heroes of the Skies' program. He stated, 'They always arrived after the action. We would be returning home exhausted, only to see these 60 aircraft flying overhead in close formation, wondering where the enemy was. They had already gone home.' He further added, 'They claimed 20, 25, or 30 aircraft shot down, but we didn't see any aircraft shot down. The claims made by Big Wing seemed exaggerated.' Another pilot described 'Big Wing' as 'absolute nonsense.' Bader's story became well-known and was later adapted into a film. He lost both legs in an air crash in the 1930s, but he overcame this disability and returned to flying. Many airmen would lose consciousness due to the G-forces, which caused blood to rush from their heads to their legs. However, because of his 1931 accident, Bader did not have this problem and could push himself and his aircraft to the limit. After crashing in 1931, it seemed unlikely that Sir Douglas Bader would survive, let alone fly again. While performing low-flying aerobatics, his aircraft crashed when the wingtip touched the ground, resulting in the amputation of both legs – one above and one below the knee. Despite this, he rejoined the RAF in 1939 when war broke out and became a squadron leader within two years. In 1941, he was shot down and captured in France. The German forces treated Bader with respect. When he lost his prosthetic leg while bailing out, the Germans allowed the British to drop in a replacement. Subsequently, he made numerous escape attempts, leading the Germans to threaten to take away his legs. Bader once escaped from a hospital by tying sheets together but was betrayed by a hospital worker, who was later sentenced to 20 years in prison by French authorities. In 1942, he escaped from Stalag Luft III with three others but was found a few days later. The Germans were so concerned about his attempts that they created a poster describing him and his walk to help the public identify him if he escaped again. Eventually, he was sent to Colditz, where he remained until the end of the war, continually trying to escape. After bailing out over France in the summer of 1941 and being captured, he became a constant problem for the enemy. He repeatedly escaped with other Britons from various camps, evading the Germans for extended periods and almost reaching Britain on several occasions. Despite further attempts to escape from Colditz, he remained there until the war's end. The 'Heroes of the Skies' documentary series began airing on Channel 5 and consists of six one-hour episodes. Bader conceived the 'Big Wing' tactic and convinced Air Vice-Marshal Sir Trafford Leigh-Mallory, the commander in charge of the Midlands' defense, of its effectiveness. However, Air Vice-Marshal Keith Park, responsible for London and the south east, preferred smaller, faster teams to attack the Germans. Despite Park's disagreement, Leigh-Mallory replaced him and implemented 'Big Wing' more widely. The tactic continues to have supporters among other veterans. Sir Alan Smith, 95, Bader's wingman with at least 20 confirmed kills, stated, 'It was very logical and very sensible.' He added, 'He was a marvelous leader, a brilliant pilot, a dead shot, and everything you could ask for.' In tribute to his friend, who died in 1982, Sir Alan said, 'He didn't just save my life; he saved a hell of a lot of lives.'
translated_content: Sir Douglas Bader va ser el pilot britànic més celebrat de la Segona Guerra Mundial. Tot i perdre les dues cames en un accident d'avió, va continuar servint i va ajudar els aliats a derrotar els alemanys a l'aire. No obstant això, un nou documental confirma la seva brillantor aèria, però desafia les tàctiques de 'Big Wing' de Sir Douglas Bader, que implicaven l'ús de fins a 60 avions de la RAF per aclapara l'enemic en una gran formació. Els veterans que van servir amb ell suggereixen que aquest enfocament era lent i posava en perill altres pilots. El comandant d'ala Tom Neil, de 93 anys, receptor de la Creu de Vol Distingit i Barra amb 15 morts confirmades, va participar en el programa 'Heroes of the Skies'. Va declarar: 'Sempre arribaven després de l'acció. Tornàvem a casa esgotats, només per veure aquests 60 avions volant per sobre en formació tancada, preguntant-nos on era l'enemic. Ja havien tornat a casa'. Va afegir a més: 'Afirmaven que havien abatut 20, 25 o 30 avions, però no vam veure cap avió abatut. Les afirmacions fetes per Big Wing semblaven exagerades'. Tot i això, a causa del seu accident del 1931, Bader no tenia aquest problema i podia portar-se a ell mateix i el seu avió al límit. Després de l'accident del 1931, semblava poc probable que Sir Douglas Bader sobrevisqués, i molt menys que tornés a volar. Mentre feia acrobàcies a baixa altitud, el seu avió es va estavellar quan la punta de l'ala va tocar a terra, fet que va provocar l'amputació de les dues cames: una per sobre i una per sota del genoll. Posteriorment, va fer nombrosos intents de fuga, cosa que va fer que els alemanys amenacessin d'emportar-se les cames. Bader va escapar una vegada d'un hospital lligant llençols, però va ser traït per un treballador de l'hospital, que més tard va ser condemnat a 20 anys de presó per les autoritats franceses. El 1942, va escapar de Stalag Luft III amb tres altres, però va ser trobat uns dies després. Els alemanys estaven tan preocupats pels seus intents que van crear un cartell que el descrivia a ell i la seva manera de caminar per ajudar el públic a identificar-lo si tornava a escapar. Finalment, va ser enviat a Colditz, on va romandre fins al final de la guerra, intentant escapar contínuament. Després de saltar en paracaigudes sobre França l'estiu de 1941 i ser capturat, es va convertir en un problema constant per a l'enemic. Va escapar repetidament amb altres britànics de diversos camps, evadint els alemanys durant períodes prolongats i gairebé arribant a Gran Bretanya en diverses ocasions. Malgrat altres intents d'escapar de Colditz, hi va romandre fins al final de la guerra. La sèrie documental 'Heroes of the Skies' va començar a emetre's a Channel 5 i consta de sis episodis d'una hora. Bader va concebre la tàctica 'Big Wing' i va convèncer el vicemariscal de l'aire Sir Trafford Leigh-Mallory, el comandant encarregat de la defensa de les Midlands, de la seva eficàcia. No obstant això, el vicemariscal de l'aire Keith Park, responsable de Londres i el sud-est, preferia equips més petits i ràpids per atacar els alemanys. Malgrat el desacord de Park, Leigh-Mallory el va substituir i va implementar 'Big Wing' de manera més àmplia. La tàctica continua tenint partidaris entre altres veterans. Sir Alan Smith, de 95 anys, company d'ala de Bader amb almenys 20 morts confirmades, va declarar: 'Era molt lògic i molt sensat'. Va afegir: 'Era un líder meravellós, un pilot brillant, un tirador excel·lent, i tot el que es podia demanar'. En homenatge al seu amic, que va morir el 1982, Sir Alan va dir: 'No només em va salvar la vida; va salvar un munt de vides'.

article_content: A driver who ingested approximately 70 lines of cocaine before fatally hitting a passer-by has been sentenced to life imprisonment. Stephen Freye, 22, intentionally drove his car in search of someone to hit late at night and targeted a young chef walking home. Kyle Griffith, a 25-year-old father, was walking on the sidewalk after finishing work at a restaurant when Freye deliberately steered his car towards him, resulting in his immediate death. Freye claimed to have been hallucinating after consuming around 10 grams of cocaine over a weekend. During the trial at Cardiff Crown Court, Freye admitted to police at the scene: 'I was told to kill a stranger.' Freye, from Roath, Cardiff, pleaded not guilty to murder but was convicted after a two-week trial. The judge sentenced him to life in prison, stipulating a minimum of 13 years to be served. Mr. Justice MacDuff stated that he had reviewed impact statements from Kyle’s mother, step-father, and sister. He told Freye: 'They are profoundly distressing. Kyle was an exceptionally kind and valuable man whose life has been tragically cut short.' 'He was an innocent young man and father, simply walking home after an evening in town, when you struck him.' 'You were in a psychotic state, hallucinating and hearing the voice of your drug supplier instructing you to kill.' 'You voluntarily consumed drugs over a three-day period, fully aware of their effects.' 'You succumbed to your addiction, but the decision was yours alone, and you bear the responsibility.' 'Kyle was a remarkable young man, deeply loved, with a promising future ahead of him.' 'He was diligent and harbored no ill will towards anyone. He had a young daughter whom he adored, and he positively influenced many lives.' 'His sister had to commemorate her 21st birthday just four days after her brother’s passing, transforming what should have been a celebration into a time of mourning.' 'You informed the jury that you were genuinely sorry, but your remorse was solely for yourself. Your words rang hollow, and your demeanor in court today demonstrated no contrition.' 'You will have to live with the consequences of your actions for the remainder of your life.' Prosecutor Huw Evans stated: 'Freye had ingested cocaine and experienced hallucinations shortly before intentionally driving into Mr. Griffith.' 'He told police that the moment he saw his victim, he heard voices telling him his own family would die if he didn’t hit him.' 'He said he acted without thinking, assuming that running him over would resolve everything.' 'He deliberately drove at him with the intention to kill or cause severe harm.' Mr. Griffith was a chef at the Cardiff Arts Institute and the father of a four-year-old girl named Emma. The jury was shown videos made by Freye in his apartment, depicting him taking cocaine and apparently listening for the voices he claimed to hear. The dark videos showed him sitting, staring at the camera and looking around the room. Freye claimed he was driving to a police station in his Fiat Cinquecento to report the voices when he saw Kyle on the side of the road in January of that year. He denied murdering Kyle but admitted manslaughter, asserting that he was suffering from a mental abnormality at the time. Freye told the jury: 'The cocaine was so irresistible that when I obtained it from the dealer, I immediately began snorting it from the bag on the way back.' 'I was completely enslaved to it.' 'The voices had complete control over me. As soon as I saw him, the voices spoke.' 'And as soon as I heard them, I turned the car—I didn’t have time to think.' Speaking outside the court, a spokesperson for Kyle’s family said: 'No punishment can ever bring Kyle back or alleviate the pain of his tragic and sudden death.' 'However, we are grateful that some measure of justice has been served today.'

Parlant a les portes del jutjat, un portaveu de la família de Kyle va dir: 'Cap càstig pot retornar mai a Kyle ni alleujar el dolor de la seva tràgica i sobtada mort.' article_content: A government official stated in a radio interview on Tuesday that hundreds of dolphins that washed up on Peruvian shores died of natural causes. Peruvian Production Minister Gladys Triveno told RPP Radio, 'One thing we can confirm is that the deaths of the dolphins were not caused by any human activity, which is a very important finding.' Government investigators have also ruled out bacteria or viruses as potential causes, Triveno said, adding that further details would be included in a report from the Sea Institute of Peru, which was released on Tuesday. 'It is due to natural causes, a natural death. The report also explains the process of natural selection, suggesting that the more prepared dolphins are the ones that will survive,' Triveno stated. 'This happens periodically and not only in Peru, but also in New Zealand, Australia, and other countries where similar phenomena occur.' According to the report, authorities sent specimens to at least four laboratories for extensive testing. The results excluded several possible causes of death, including hunger, interaction with fishermen, pesticides, bacterial infections, viral infections, and heavy metals contamination. The appearance of nearly 900 dead dolphins in a 220-kilometer (137-mile) area in northern Peru this year, along with the deaths of thousands of pelicans in Peru and neighboring Chile, has raised concerns among local residents and environmentalists. At least one Peruvian environmental group has suggested that loud noises from nearby oil exploration could be responsible for the dolphins' deaths. 'We see air bubbles in their bodies caused by heavy pressure. These animals are underwater holding their breath, facing a sudden and violent noise. They release nitrogen, forming bubbles that destroy living cells,' Carlos Yaipen-Llanos of the Scientific Organization for the Conservation of Aquatic Animals told CNN en Español this month. Government officials have rejected this assessment, arguing it lacks evidence. The report indicated that the dead dolphins began washing ashore before the seismic activity started, and similar past activity has not been linked to marine deaths. This month, Peruvian authorities attributed the deaths of more than 5,000 marine birds to warm waters off the coast, according to the Peruvian Ministry of Environment. The Peruvian Ministry of Environment, citing the state-run Andina news agency, assured the public that seafood remains safe to eat and encouraged continued support for local fishermen. The report recommended several actions, including creating a task force involving multiple agencies to implement programs for the marine ecosystem's care, and launching an awareness campaign for the general public about Peruvian ocean life and its conservation. The dolphin deaths in Peru represent the third set of significant strandings in recent months. In February, 179 dolphins, including 108 found dead, washed ashore in Cape Cod, Massachusetts, according to the International Fund for Animal Welfare. Marine biologists are still investigating the cause of these deaths. In early March, amateur video from a beach in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, showed over 30 dolphins on shore. All of those dolphins were safely returned to the sea.

La mort de dofins a Perú representa el tercer conjunt de varaments significatius en els darrers mesos. article_content: Alice Rambridge, a nine-year-old girl, has a rare condition called agenesis of the corpus callosum (ACC) that prevents her from experiencing pain or shedding tears. This unusual condition means that the two halves of Alice's brain aren't connected the way they should be. ACC is so rare that only about 50 cases have been documented worldwide. Even when Alice suffers burns, she doesn't react due to her extremely high pain threshold. Despite dealing with illnesses like colds and chicken pox, Alice has never cried and can't describe pain. Her mother, Lindsay, 37, notices Alice falls and gets hurt like other children, but without any reaction. She even wondered if Alice had tear ducts. When hospitalized, Alice seems confused because she doesn't feel anything is wrong. Once, she touched a hot stove and continued playing while her mother treated the burn. Another time, her forehead was bruised, but Alice didn't seem bothered. She was diagnosed with ACC at 19 months old. The condition means the structure connecting the brain's hemispheres is either partially or completely absent. Alice also experiences difficulties understanding social cues due to the disorder affecting her brain development. Lindsay, from Preston, Lancashire, ensures Alice is in a safe environment and avoids situations that might confuse her. Symptoms of ACC include vision issues, low pain perception, delayed toilet training, feeding difficulties, and seizures. Lindsay is now fundraising to buy Alice a specialized bed costing £7,000, which social services won't cover. She describes Alice as an amazing, loving, inspirational, courageous, and encouraging girl who always smiles, despite her challenges. She wants to make Alice's life as easy and comfortable as possible. Donations can be made at www.justgiving.com/SmileyAlice/ or https://www.facebook.com/Alicesfund.

article_content: Scientists have made progress in the fight against obesity by identifying cells that can transform unhealthy white fat into beneficial brown fat. These cells, known as ILC2s, play a key role in converting the type of fat that leads to weight gain (white fat) into fat that helps the body burn extra calories (brown fat). Researchers in the United States suggest that manipulating the body's metabolic processes where these ILC2 cells operate could offer a new strategy for tackling obesity. This discovery may lead to innovative treatments for diseases linked to obesity. The study, conducted by scientists at Weill Cornell Medical College in New York, revealed that ILC2s promote the conversion of white fat into brown fat. The researchers believe their findings could pave the way for the development of an anti-obesity pill, potentially offering protection against obesity-related illnesses. The human body contains two types of fat tissue. White fat accumulates when we consume more calories than we burn, leading to weight gain. Brown fat, on the other hand, burns excess energy, helping to reduce the amount of white fat. The research indicated that ILC2s, found within white fat tissue, contribute to weight management by boosting energy levels. They facilitate the transformation of harmful white fat into beneficial brown fat, thereby aiding in the prevention of conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, and other life-threatening ailments associated with obesity. Previous research has linked impaired ILC2 function to obesity in mice. However, more recent studies on white fat tissue have shown that similar abnormalities are present in humans and affect energy metabolism. The latest study discovered that ILC2s stimulate the 'browning' of white fat in response to a signaling protein called IL-33. When mice were injected with IL-33, the researchers observed an increase in ILC2s within their white fat, resulting in calorie burning and weight loss compared to untreated mice. Professor David Artis and his team at Weill Cornell Medical College conducted this research. In England, obesity affects one in four adults, and projections indicate that these numbers could rise to 60% of men and 50% of women by 2050. The annual cost of obesity and diabetes to the UK is currently over £5 billion and is expected to increase to £50 billion in the next 36 years. Beyond just weight loss, a drug that converts white fat into brown fat could also lower the risk of developing type 2 diabetes and provide protection against heart disease. article_content: According to documents leaked by former National Security Agency employee Edward Snowden, the U.S. government allegedly monitored prominent American Muslims using the same methods employed for suspected terrorists. Glenn Greenwald and Murtaza Hussain, writing in The Intercept, reported that Snowden's documents indicated that at least five American Muslims were subjected to governmental surveillance between 2002 and 2008. The names appearing on a spreadsheet, believed to list individuals under digital surveillance by the NSA, CIA, or FBI, include: Faisal Gill, a Republican Party member and lawyer; Asim Ghafoor, an attorney; Hooshang Amirahmadi, a professor of international relations; Agha Saeed, a Muslim civil liberties advocate; and Nihad Awad, the executive director of the Council on American-Islamic Affairs. The spreadsheet reportedly contained over 7,000 email addresses, including those of foreigners linked to terrorist organizations and U.S. citizens suspected of terrorist activities. However, the list also included the five prominent Muslim-Americans, none of whom have ever faced terrorism charges or accusations, and all of whom deny any connection to terrorism. Faisal Gill and Asim Ghafoor told CNN that they believed they were targeted solely because of their Muslim faith, which they consider a violation of their rights. Gill stated he could think of no other reason. Ghafoor echoed this sentiment. Gill, who previously held a security clearance while working at the Department of Homeland Security, expressed shock, stating that nothing in his background would warrant suspicion of terrorist acts. Ghafoor, a civil rights attorney who has represented clients in terrorism-related cases, questioned the government's rationale for monitoring his communications with his clients, asking what information they could use in court. Ghafoor noted that the government appeared to be monitoring his Yahoo email account, not his law firm email. He humorously remarked that the agents monitoring his Yahoo account would find little of value. Gill, a Navy veteran and former senior policy advisor at the Department of Homeland Security under President George W. Bush, also worked as a spokesman for the American Muslim Council. The council's founder, Aldurahman M. Alamoudi, was imprisoned in 2004 for activities related to terrorism. However, the alleged surveillance of Gill occurred between 2006 and 2008, after he left the council and was a Republican nominee for the Virginia House of Delegates, according to Greenwald. Gill stated that he barely knew Alamoudi and disclosed his prior employment with the Muslim council to the U.S. government, which subsequently granted him a security clearance. He argued that while surveillance is necessary, there must be a valid reason for it, and he believed there was no justification in his case. Gill criticized the high success rate of warrant applications to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance (FISA) Court, calling it 'ridiculous' and suggesting something is amiss. He told The Intercept that he believed his emails were intercepted because he is Muslim, pointing out that other lawyers who have represented individuals associated with terrorism have not been targeted. In a joint statement, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and the Justice Department refuted the claim that the U.S. government conducts surveillance based on political views, religion, or activism. The statement asserted that the U.S. does not monitor communications to suppress criticism or disadvantage individuals based on ethnicity, race, gender, sexual orientation, or religion. The statement further explained that surveillance of U.S. citizens requires a FISA Court order, issued only when probable cause exists, based on specific facts, that the person is an agent of a foreign power, a terrorist, a spy, or someone taking orders from a foreign power. However, The Intercept reported that at least one of the five American Muslims was monitored without a FISA warrant. Additionally, one of the documents provided by Snowden to The Intercept contained an example memo requesting FISA surveillance, using the derogatory placeholder name 'Mohammed Raghead.' An NSA spokeswoman stated that such insulting language would not be permitted in its training documents. CAIR, the largest Muslim civil liberties group in the U.S., led by Awad, demanded a full accounting of government spying on American Muslims, characterizing it as an 'outrageous continuation of civil rights era surveillance of minority community leadership.'

Glenn Greenwald i Murtaza Hussain, escrivint a The Intercept, van informar que els documents de Snowden indicaven que almenys cinc musulmans americans van ser sotmesos a vigilància governamental entre el 2002 i el 2008. Els noms que apareixen en un full de càlcul, que es creu que enumera individus sota vigilància digital per la NSA, la CIA o l'FBI, inclouen: Faisal Gill, membre del Partit Republicà i advocat; Asim Ghafoor, advocat; Hooshang Amirahmadi, professor de relacions internacionals; Agha Saeed, defensor de les llibertats civils musulmanes; i Nihad Awad, el director executiu del Consell d'Afers Islàmics Americans. Segons s'informa, el full de càlcul contenia més de 7.000 adreces de correu electrònic, incloses les d'estrangers vinculats a organitzacions terroristes i ciutadans nord-americans sospitosos d'activitats terroristes. No obstant això, la llista també incloïa els cinc musulmans americans destacats, cap dels quals mai s'ha enfrontat a càrrecs o acusacions de terrorisme, i tots neguen qualsevol connexió amb el terrorisme. Faisal Gill i Asim Ghafoor van dir a CNN que creien que van ser objectiu únicament a causa de la seva fe musulmana, cosa que consideren una violació dels seus drets. Gill va declarar que no podia pensar en cap altre motiu. Ghafoor es va fer ressò d'aquest sentiment. Gill, que anteriorment tenia una autorització de seguretat mentre treballava al Departament de Seguretat Nacional, va expressar sorpresa i va declarar que res en els seus antecedents justificaria la sospita d'actes terroristes. Ghafoor, un advocat de drets civils que ha representat clients en casos relacionats amb el terrorisme, va qüestionar la justificació del govern per controlar les seves comunicacions amb els seus clients, preguntant quina informació podrien utilitzar al tribunal. Ghafoor va assenyalar que el govern semblava estar controlant el seu compte de correu electrònic de Yahoo, no el correu electrònic del seu despatx d'advocats. Va comentar amb humor que els agents que controlaven el seu compte de Yahoo trobarien poc valor. Gill, un veterà de la Marina i antic assessor polític principal al Departament de Seguretat Nacional sota el president George W. Bush, també va treballar com a portaveu del Consell Musulmà Americà. El fundador del consell, Aldurahman M. Alamoudi, va ser empresonat el 2004 per activitats relacionades amb el terrorisme. No obstant això, la presumpta vigilància de Gill es va produir entre el 2006 i el 2008, després que va deixar el consell i fos candidat republicà a la Cambra de Delegats de Virgínia, segons Greenwald. Gill va declarar que gairebé no coneixia Alamoudi i va revelar el seu anterior treball amb el consell musulmà al govern dels EUA, que posteriorment li va concedir una autorització de seguretat. Va argumentar que, tot i que la vigilància és necessària, hi ha d'haver un motiu vàlid per a això, i va creure que no hi havia cap justificació en el seu cas. Gill va criticar l'alta taxa d'èxit de les sol·licituds d'ordres judicials al Tribunal de Vigilància d'Intel·ligència Estrangera (FISA), qualificant-la de 'ridícula' i suggerint que hi ha alguna cosa que no funciona. Va dir a The Intercept que creia que els seus correus electrònics van ser interceptats perquè és musulmà, assenyalant que altres advocats que han representat persones associades amb el terrorisme no han estat objectiu. En una declaració conjunta, l'Oficina del Director d'Intel·ligència Nacional i el Departament de Justícia van refutar la afirmació que el govern dels EUA du a terme vigilància basada en opinions polítiques, religió o activisme. La declaració va afirmar que els EUA no controlen les comunicacions per suprimir les crítiques o posar a les persones en desavantatge en funció de l'ètnia, la raça, el gènere, l'orientació sexual o la religió. La declaració va explicar a més que la vigilància dels ciutadans nord-americans requereix una ordre judicial de la FISA, emesa només quan existeix una causa probable, basada en fets específics, que la persona sigui un agent d'una potència estrangera, un terrorista, un espia o algú que rebi ordres d'una potència estrangera. No obstant això, The Intercept va informar que almenys un dels cinc musulmans americans va ser controlat sense una ordre judicial de la FISA. A més, un dels documents proporcionats per Snowden a The Intercept contenia un memoràndum d'exemple que sol·licitava la vigilància de la FISA, utilitzant el nom reservat despectiu 'Mohammed Raghead'. Una portaveu de la NSA va declarar que no es permetria un llenguatge tan insultant en els seus documents de formació. CAIR, el grup de llibertats civils musulmanes més gran dels EUA, dirigit per Awad, va exigir un balanç complet de l'espionatge del govern als musulmans americans, caracteritzant-ho com una 'continuació escandalosa de la vigilància de l'era dels drets civils del lideratge de la comunitat minoritària'.

article_content: Mexico City (CNN) -- Protesters marched and filled the main square of Mexico City on Sunday, criticizing the candidate widely considered the front-runner in next month's presidential elections. Enrique Peña Nieto, the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) candidate, holds a lead in opinion polls. The PRI governed for approximately 70 years before losing the presidency in 2000. Demonstrators argue that his victory would represent a setback for democracy in Mexico. 'I'm here because I'm really angry with what's going on in my country. I think it's not fair,' said Adrian Garcia, 34, a protester. He wore a white T-shirt displaying 'Yo Soy 132' ('I am 132'), the name of a burgeoning protest movement that Peña Nieto indirectly helped to create. After students booed the candidate at a recent campaign rally, Peña Nieto dismissed them as outsiders, claiming they were brought in by political operatives to stir up trouble. Three days later, a YouTube video surfaced featuring 131 students displaying their university identification cards and stating, 'We are students from Ibero. ... Nobody forced us to do anything.' The 11-minute video quickly went viral. Social media posts promoting protests nationwide have used the video as a starting point, employing the hashtag '#YoSoy132' on Twitter and Facebook. Sunday's protests in Mexico City drew participation from not only students but also teachers, unions, and various political organizations. The demonstrations were scheduled to coincide with the final televised debate before the presidential election, slated for July 1. Similar, albeit smaller, demonstrations took place in other Mexican cities. Garcia mentioned that he voted for leftist candidate Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador in the previous election. Lopez Obrador, who never conceded after officials declared Felipe Calderon the winner of Mexico's 2006 election, has referred to himself as 'the legitimate president of Mexico.' The former Mexico City mayor is once again a candidate. 'They are touching on a fundamental theme that has to do with the pretension of dominating the country through the almost absolute control of the media,' Lopez Obrador commented recently about the protesters. He and other opponents have accused Peña Nieto of receiving preferential treatment from the media even before the campaign officially began. Peña Nieto, who served as governor of the State of Mexico from 2005 to 2011, has denied these accusations and stated that he respects the youth protests against him. CNNMexico.com and Miguel Marquez contributed to this report.
translated_content: Ciutat de Mèxic (CNN) -- Diumenge, manifestants van marxar i omplir la plaça principal de la Ciutat de Mèxic, criticant el candidat àmpliament considerat com el favorit a les eleccions presidencials del mes vinent. Enrique Peña Nieto, el candidat del Partit Revolucionari Institucional (PRI), manté un avantatge a les enquestes d'opinió. El PRI va governar durant aproximadament 70 anys abans de perdre la presidència l'any 2000. Els manifestants argumenten que la seva victòria representaria un retrocés per a la democràcia a Mèxic. 'Estic aquí perquè estic molt enfadat amb el que està passant al meu país. Crec que no és just', va dir Adrian Garcia, de 34 anys, un manifestant. Portava una samarreta blanca amb el lema 'Yo Soy 132' ('Jo sóc 132'), el nom d'un moviment de protesta emergent que Peña Nieto va ajudar a crear indirectament. Després que els estudiants esbronquessin el candidat en un míting de campanya recent, Peña Nieto els va desestimar com a forasters, al·legant que van ser portats per operatius polítics per causar problemes. Tres dies després, va aparèixer un vídeo a YouTube amb 131 estudiants que mostraven els seus carnets d'identificació universitaris i afirmaven: 'Som estudiants d'Ibero. ... Ningú no ens va obligar a fer res.' El vídeo d'11 minuts es va fer viral ràpidament. Les publicacions a les xarxes socials que promouen protestes a tot el país han utilitzat el vídeo com a punt de partida, fent servir l'etiqueta '#YoSoy132' a Twitter i Facebook. Les protestes de diumenge a la Ciutat de Mèxic van comptar amb la participació no només d'estudiants, sinó també de professors, sindicats i diverses organitzacions polítiques. Les manifestacions van ser programades per coincidir amb l'últim debat televisat abans de les eleccions presidencials, previstes per a l'1 de juliol. Es van fer manifestacions similars, tot i que més petites, en altres ciutats mexicanes. Garcia va mencionar que va votar pel candidat d'esquerres, Andrés Manuel López Obrador, a les eleccions anteriors. López Obrador, que mai no va cedir després que els funcionaris declaressin Felipe Calderón guanyador de les eleccions de Mèxic del 2006, s'ha referit a si mateix com 'el president legítim de Mèxic'. L'exalcalde de la Ciutat de Mèxic torna a ser candidat. 'Estan tocant un tema fonamental que té a veure amb la pretensió de dominar el país mitjançant el control gairebé absolut dels mitjans de comunicació', va comentar López Obrador recentment sobre els manifestants. Ell i altres opositors han acusat Peña Nieto de rebre un tracte preferencial per part dels mitjans de comunicació fins i tot abans que la campanya comencés oficialment. Peña Nieto, que va ser governador de l'Estat de Mèxic del 2005 al 2011, ha negat aquestes acusacions i ha afirmat que respecta les protestes juvenils en contra seva. CNNMexico.com i Miguel Marquez van contribuir a aquest informe.

article_content: Mbabane, Swaziland (CNN) -- We met her in the car park of a small shopping mall on the edge of Mbabane, Swaziland's capital. She was too shy to get out of the car her friend had brought her in, too nervous about who might see, or what might be overheard. She told us that she knew an isolated place where we could talk. Ten minutes later we were in scrubland standing by the rubble and remains of someone's home. Here Nelsie - not her real name - stopped fiddling with her plastic necklace and started looking me in the eye, but even that appeared to take considerable effort. She told me that for the last two years, since both her parents died in a car crash, she has lived on the periphery, isolated from her remaining family and society. 'Right now I don't feel that I am a human being,' she confessed. 'Right now I am scared to greet my family because if I say that I am a prostitute all of the people will just say that I am a prostitute'. She wants us to know that this was not her first choice; she did try to find work. 'Here in Swaziland there are no jobs,' she says. The necklace fiddling starts again. 'I have no choice but to be a sex worker; whether I like it or not, I must do that'. Tucked away in one corner of Swaziland's annual International Trade Fair, we found the HIV/AIDS stands. It was an unusual addition at a trade fair, but so was the large number of children who had come here for a day out with their parents; there was barely a businessman or woman in sight. These stands are testimony to a tragic situation; Swaziland, now known as Eswatini, continues to struggle with a high rate of HIV and AIDS. A staggering one in four people in Eswatini have HIV/AIDS. Read related: Opinion: How to end AIDS. At one stand, Zelda Nhlabatsi, who runs the Family Life Association of Swaziland, is trying to raise awareness about the disease. The free condoms on her table seemed to have attracted quite a crowd. Her organization offers support and education to sex workers, and she believes there is a growing number of women, just like Nelsie, who are turning to prostitution because of the country's financial woes. 'Everyone needs food; those are basic needs, and the unemployment rate is quite high, so sex work for most people is a livelihood, you know'. And the situation is likely to get worse, she warned me. 'You are going to be seeing more and more people engaging in different kinds of work, including sex work'. Eswatini's government blames the financial woes on a drop in income from the Southern African Customs Union following a new tariff deal. Organizations like the IMF have urged Eswatini's government to cut its bloated civil service, reduce spending, and attract foreign investors. At the height of the crisis, antiretrovirals were scarce, cancer treatment was stopped, and schools were closed. According to the African Development Bank, youth unemployment in Eswatini is currently over fifty percent. Political parties may be banned here, but the unions are emboldened and have led angry protests on the streets. Read related: South African girl brides abducted as fabled HIV cure. South Africa's President Zuma offered some financial assistance after the IMF refused Eswatini a loan. A three hundred and fifty-five million dollar bailout was agreed upon, but as of the time of reporting, disbursement details remain unclear. Majozi Sithole, Eswatini's Finance Minister, told me, 'Right now I am not sure; we are waiting for the South Africans to engage with us about whether that money is still available or not, and if it is, then we will gladly take it. It will assist us in meeting some of the fiscal challenges that we are currently facing, but if it is not available, then we are already taking steps to say let's look at what we have'. Critics of King Mswati believe he and his array of wives have contributed to the financial demise of this small landlocked kingdom. There are reports of shopping trips to Europe, a private jet from a private sponsor, and plans for a second international airport for a country with just over one million people. However, the country's Finance Minister denies this. 'I can assure you that his Majesty, the Royal Family, never overspend on what they have been allocated. If there are any challenges, they are in other ministries,' he told me when we met him in his office. 'Those who would blame it on his Majesty do not have the information; he never overspends. We discuss the fiscal challenges on a weekly basis; I brief him, he has concerns, and he will, as he did this year, say whatever you work on, don't even increase my budget because I understand the fiscal situation'. Read related: India's sex slaves face lifelong cycle of abuse. Sitting on a block of rubble with the sun fast descending behind her, Nelsie told me she always wants the men she meets to use condoms. 'I am HIV positive; I contracted HIV through rape. Before I was raped, I was HIV negative because I did not like to sleep with a man without a condom'. She and around 20 other women working in the neighborhood hide in the shadows of the night waiting for a car to pull up. To feed herself, she says she has to have sex with twenty men in two weeks, 'but sometimes in a day I used to sleep with five or six men'. Like many people who are struggling to make a living in Eswatini, there is no respite or prospect of a bailout. 'In this work we will die, so while they do not think about us, I do not think they are making an improvement in this country. We know that our economy is down, but they must try, whether to supply us with food, whether to supply us with work.'
translated_content: Mbabane, Eswatini (CNN) -- La vam conèixer a l'aparcament d'un petit centre comercial als afores de Mbabane, la capital d'Eswatini. Era massa tímida per sortir del cotxe on la seva amiga l'havia portat, massa nerviosa per qui la pogués veure o què es pogués sentir. Ens va dir que coneixia un lloc aïllat on podríem parlar. Deu minuts més tard, érem en un terreny erm al costat de la runa i les restes de la casa d'algú. Aquí, la Nelsie -no és el seu nom real- va deixar de jugar amb el seu collaret de plàstic i em va començar a mirar als ulls, però fins i tot això semblava requerir un esforç considerable. Em va dir que durant els darrers dos anys, des que els seus pares van morir en un accident de cotxe, ha viscut a la perifèria, aïllada de la seva família i societat restants. 'Ara mateix no sento que sigui un ésser humà', va confessar. 'Ara mateix tinc por de saludar la meva família perquè si dic que sóc prostituta, tothom dirà que sóc prostituta'. Vol que sapiguem que aquesta no va ser la seva primera opció; va intentar trobar feina. 'Aquí a Eswatini no hi ha feines', diu. El joc amb el collaret comença de nou. 'No tinc més remei que ser treballadora sexual; vulgui o no, ho he de fer'. Amagat en un racó de la Fira Internacional anual d'Eswatini, vam trobar els estands de VIH/SIDA. Va ser una addició inusual a una fira, però també ho va ser el gran nombre de nens que havien vingut a passar el dia amb els seus pares; gairebé no hi havia cap empresari o dona de negocis a la vista. Aquests estands són un testimoni d'una situació tràgica; Eswatini continua lluitant amb una alta taxa de VIH i SIDA. Una xifra sorprenent d'una de cada quatre persones a Eswatini té VIH/SIDA. Llegeix relacionat: Opinió: Com acabar amb la SIDA. En un estand, Zelda Nhlabatsi, que dirigeix l'Associació de Vida Familiar d'Eswatini, està intentant conscienciar sobre la malaltia. Els preservatius gratuïts a la seva taula semblaven haver atret força gent. La seva organització ofereix suport i educació a les treballadores sexuals, i creu que hi ha un nombre creixent de dones, igual que la Nelsie, que es dediquen a la prostitució a causa dels problemes financers del país. 'Tothom necessita menjar; aquestes són necessitats bàsiques, i la taxa d'atur és força alta, així que el treball sexual per a la majoria de la gent és un mitjà de vida, ja saps'. I és probable que la situació empitjori, em va advertir. 'Veureu cada vegada més gent que es dedica a diferents tipus de feina, incloent-hi el treball sexual'. El govern d'Eswatini culpa els problemes financers a una disminució dels ingressos de la Unió Duanera de l'Àfrica Austral després d'un nou acord aranzelari. Organitzacions com l'FMI han instat el govern d'Eswatini a reduir la seva inflada administració pública, reduir la despesa i atraure inversors estrangers. En el punt àlgid de la crisi, els antiretrovirals eren escassos, el tractament contra el càncer es va aturar i les escoles van tancar. Segons el Banc Africà de Desenvolupament, l'atur juvenil a Eswatini supera actualment el cinquanta per cent. Els partits polítics poden estar prohibits aquí, però els sindicats estan envalentits i han liderat protestes furioses als carrers. Llegeix relacionat: Nenes núvies sud-africanes segrestades com a cura mítica del VIH. El president de Sud-àfrica, Zuma, va oferir certa assistència financera després que l'FMI negués un préstec a Eswatini. Es va acordar un rescat de tres-cents cinquanta-cinc milions de dòlars, però, en el moment d'escriure aquest informe, els detalls del desemborsament no estan clars. Majozi Sithole, el ministre de Finances d'Eswatini, em va dir: 'Ara mateix no n'estic segur; estem esperant que els sud-africans es posin en contacte amb nosaltres sobre si aquests diners encara estan disponibles o no, i si ho estan, llavors els agafarem de bon grat. Ens ajudarà a afrontar alguns dels problemes fiscals que estem afrontant actualment, però si no estan disponibles, ja estem prenent mesures per dir mirem què tenim'. Els crítics del rei Mswati creuen que ell i la seva sèrie d'esposes han contribuït a la desaparició financera d'aquest petit regne sense litoral. Hi ha informes de viatges de compres a Europa, un jet privat d'un patrocinador privat i plans per a un segon aeroport internacional per a un país amb poc més d'un milió de persones. Tot i això, el ministre de Finances del país ho nega. 'Us puc assegurar que Sa Majestat, la Família Reial, mai no gasten massa en allò que se'ls ha assignat. Si hi ha algun problema, és en altres ministeris', em va dir quan ens vam reunir amb ell al seu despatx. 'Aquells que culpen a Sa Majestat no tenen la informació; ell mai no gasta massa. Parlem dels problemes fiscals setmanalment; l'informo, té preocupacions i ell, com va fer aquest any, dirà que feu el que feu, ni tan sols augmenteu el meu pressupost perquè entenc la situació fiscal'. Llegeix relacionat: Les esclaves sexuals de l'Índia s'enfronten a un cicle d'abusos de per vida. Asseguda en un bloc de runa amb el sol baixant ràpidament darrere seu, la Nelsie em va dir que sempre vol que els homes que coneix utilitzin preservatius. 'Sóc seropositiva; vaig contraure el VIH per violació. Abans de ser violada, era seronegativa perquè no m'agradava dormir amb un home sense preservatiu'. Ella i unes altres 20 dones que treballen al barri s'amaguen a les ombres de la nit esperant que un cotxe s'aturi. Per alimentar-se, diu que ha de tenir relacions sexuals amb vint homes en dues setmanes, 'però de vegades en un dia solia dormir amb cinc o sis homes'. Com moltes persones que lluiten per guanyar-se la vida a Eswatini, no hi ha treva ni perspectives de rescat. 'En aquest treball morirem, així que mentre no pensin en nosaltres, no crec que estiguin fent cap millora en aquest país. Sabem que la nostra economia està baixa, però han d'intentar-ho, ja sigui per subministrar-nos aliments, ja sigui per subministrar-nos feina.'
